title: Senior Traffic Engineer (Part-time)
description:
Hanson Values

Integrity | Commitment | Quality | Relationships | Innovation

If you’re looking for a firm that encourages innovative thinking and challenges you every day, with an opportunity to learn and advance, a career at Hanson is right for you. The belief in sustainability within our company’s practices creates a focus on client success and partnerships that are important to our communities and our environment.

If you're looking for a firm where you can contribute your expertise, mentor the next generation of engineers, and help deliver meaningful transportation improvements throughout Illinois, Hanson Professional Services may be the place for you.


We are seeking a Senior Traffic Engineer (Part-Time) to provide technical leadership, quality assurance/quality control oversight, and subject matter expertise for transportation projects. This position will support traffic engineering, roadway design, intersection design, transportation planning, and related infrastructure projects while ensuring that deliverables meet Hanson quality standards, client expectations, and applicable design criteria.


This position offers flexibility with hours based on workload and may be based in our Chicago, Lisle, Peoria, or Springfield, Illinois offices, with hybrid and remote work flexibility available.


A Day in the Life of a Senior Traffic Engineer


As a senior technical resource, you will provide independent reviews and oversight for a variety of transportation projects. Responsibilities may include:


  • Leading QA/QC reviews for traffic engineering, roadway design, transportation planning, and intersection improvement projects.
  • Reviewing plans, calculations, reports, specifications, cost estimates, and technical documents for accuracy, constructability, and compliance with applicable standards.
  • Evaluating traffic operations analyses, safety studies, traffic impact assessments, signal warrant analyses, and intersection design recommendations.
  • Reviewing roadway geometric design elements, including horizontal and vertical alignments, intersection layouts, lane configurations, and multimodal accommodations.
  • Verifying compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including MUTCD, AASHTO, ADA, and agency-specific standards.
  • Identifying design risks, conflicts, and quality concerns while recommending practical and effective solutions.
  • Providing technical guidance and mentoring to engineers, designers, and project teams.
  • Supporting project managers in maintaining quality throughout project development and delivery.
  • Participating in technical reviews, workshops, lessons learned sessions, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Assisting with proposal development, technical approaches, staffing strategies, and client presentations as needed.

Required Qualifications


  • Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering or a related engineering field.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license required.
  • Minimum 15 years of experience in traffic engineering, roadway design, transportation planning, or related transportation infrastructure projects.
  • Demonstrated experience reviewing transportation project deliverables for technical accuracy and compliance.
  • Strong knowledge of MUTCD, AASHTO, ADA, IDOT, and local agency design standards and procedures.
  • Experience conducting or reviewing traffic operations analyses, traffic studies, safety evaluations, and roadway design plans.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Qualifications


  • Illinois Professional Engineer license or ability to obtain through reciprocity.
  • Experience supporting projects for IDOT, local agencies, municipalities, and public-sector transportation clients.
  • Prior experience mentoring engineering staff and leading technical quality reviews.
  • Familiarity with traffic analysis and roadway design software utilized in transportation engineering projects.

Benefits and Perks

This is a part-time position. Work hours will vary based on project workload and business needs.

Hanson is committed to creating a workplace that values technical excellence, professional growth, collaboration, and innovation. We offer flexible work arrangements and the opportunity to contribute to meaningful transportation projects that improve the communities we serve.


This is a non-exempt position. The hourly range for this role is $70 - $85 per hour, depending on skills and experience.


Benefits

Our focus on people means we offer a generous benefits program to help you create a solid foundation for health and security throughout your career, including:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Performance bonuses

  • 401(k) with matching contribution

  • Employee Stock Ownership Plan

  • Comprehensive health & well-being plans

  • Financial wellness plans

  • Work-life balance programs

Want to know more? Visit our benefits page for all the details.

Culture

We understand that selecting a job is about more than the day-to-day tasks. It’s important to feel like you belong and safe to grow and progress along your career path. You’ll find that at Hanson. We have an inclusive, diverse workforce awaiting to connect with you and numerous opportunities to cultivate your career, including:

  • Monthly educational webinars

  • Leadership training

  • Lunch & learn development sessions

  • 24/7 access to thousands of skill-building courses

  • Mentorship opportunities

  • Award-winning internship program

  • Employee recognition

  • And so much more!

AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EEO — EMPLOYER

We do not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or agencies/staffing firms. Resumes are only accepted from recruiters and agency/staffing firms if a signed agreement is in place at the inception of the recruiting effort and authorized for a specified position.

title: Environmental Health and Safety Senior Specialist
description:
Job Summary

In support of the occupational health and safety of employees, protecting the environment, and emergency management for The Jackson Laboratory, this role is independently responsible for assessing risks, developing standards, administering policies and programs, and leading employee engagement to ensure continuous improvement and compliance with federal, state, local regulations, and internal framework.

This cross-functional role partners closely with research, production, facilities, and leadership to lead the assessment and mitigation of risks, investigate incidents, and positively influence a problem-solving culture. Success in this role requires strong follow-through, clear communication, and the ability to independently address safety concerns directly and professionally.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree required (Master's degree preferred) in Occupational Health & Safety, Public Health, Environmental Health, Environmental Sciences, or a related field such as chemistry or biology. A combination of education and experience will be considered.

  • 5 years of experience in a same or similar role required; 7 years preferred.

  • Valid driver's license required.

  • Preferred certifications include CSP, ASP/GSP, CIH, CHMM, or a comparable U.S.-recognized EHS credential.

Key Responsibilities

  • Independently develops, implements, and administers complex or Laboratory-wide EHS programs; establishes metrics and benchmarks and evaluates program effectiveness with minimal oversight.

  • Leads or represents the Laboratory during regulatory inspections and audits; interprets findings, negotiates corrective action timelines, and briefs senior leadership on regulatory exposure and remediation plans.

  • Establishes standards and procedures to ensure compliance with federal, state, and local safety regulations and internal standards; interprets emerging or ambiguous regulatory requirements for senior management.

  • Researches and benchmarks external best practices and emerging regulatory trends; recommends and drives adoption of improvements to keep Laboratory programs current and defensible.

  • Designs and oversees delivery of employee training programs for assigned area(s); mentors and coaches EHS staff on technical practice, investigation methods, and stakeholder engagement.

  • Leads investigations of complex, high-severity, or recurring incidents; performs root cause analysis and directs the development and tracking of corrective and preventive actions.

  • Analyzes trends across inspection, audit, incident, and training data to identify systemic risks and recommend program-level or organizational improvements to senior leadership.

  • Leads or serves as a key responder during emergency situations involving hazardous materials, confined space rescue, or fire/smoke incidents, and leads after-action discussions.

  • Leads cross-functional EHS initiatives and projects, coordinating resources, timelines, and communications across departments.

  • Contributes to EHS program budgeting and may assist in evaluating and procuring EHS equipment, services, or consultants.

  • Independently engages and builds trusted relationships with internal and external stakeholders without requiring day-to-day direction.

  • Serves as a designated delegate for the Site EHS Leader, representing the EHS function's priorities and making sound, timely decisions in that capacity when the Site EHS Leader is unavailable.

  • Works directly with federal, state, and local regulatory agencies, often as the Laboratory's primary point of contact for assigned program area(s).

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Advanced knowledge of environmental health & safety principles, typically acquired through a Bachelor's degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Public Health, Environmental Health, Environmental Sciences, or a related science field with at least five years of progressive EHS experience, or an Associate's degree in a related field with at least seven years of progressive EHS experience.

  • Advanced written and oral communication skills sufficient to clearly and persuasively exchange information with audiences ranging from front-line staff to senior executives and external regulators.

  • Ability to lead root cause analysis and complex incident investigations, and to translate findings into systemic, sustainable corrective actions.

  • Advanced working knowledge of applicable regulations with demonstrated success building and defending compliant, sustainable programs.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities; ability to synthesize data from multiple sources into clear, actionable recommendations for senior leadership.

  • Ability to lead technical safety audits and inspections in areas of expertise as required by policy, standards, or regulation, and effectively communicate findings to key stakeholders.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently engage and influence stakeholders, customers, and senior leadership, including building consensus and driving action without direct authority.

  • Project management skills sufficient to lead multi-stakeholder EHS initiatives from planning through completion.

  • Proficiency with common technical applications, including word processing, database management, spreadsheets, web-based tools, and presentation software.

  • Ability to serve on the Confined Space Rescue Team and Emergency Response Team.

  • Demonstrated ability to operate independently with little supervision, exercising sound judgment and prioritizing effectively in ambiguous, fast-moving, or high-pressure situations.

  • Mentoring and coaching skills; ability to develop the technical and professional capabilities of less experienced EHS staff.

  • Demonstrated ability to serve credibly as a delegate for the Site EHS Leader, representing program priorities and making decisions on the Site EHS Leader's behalf when required.

Physical Demands

Light: exerting up to 20 lbs occasionally, 0–10 lbs frequently, and negligible weights constantly.

Pay Range: $86,344 - $125,184 based on years of experience and internal equity considerations

About JAX:

The Jackson Laboratory is an independent, nonprofit biomedical research institution with a National Cancer Institute-designated Cancer Center and nearly 3,000 employees in locations across the United States (Maine, Connecticut, California), Japan and China. Its mission is to discover precise genomic solutions for disease and empower the global biomedical community in the shared quest to improve human health.

Founded in 1929, JAX applies over nine decades of expertise in genetics to increase understanding of human disease, advancing treatments and cures for cancer, neurological and immune disorders, diabetes, aging and heart disease. It models and interprets genomic complexity, integrates basic research with clinical application, educates current and future scientists, and provides critical data, tools and services to the global biomedical community. For more information, please visit ​​​​​​​.

The Jackson Laboratory provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment in all job classifications without regard to race, color, religion, age, mental disability, physical disability, medical condition, gender, sexual orientation, genetic information, ancestry, marital status, national origin, veteran status, and other classifications protected by applicable state and local non-discrimination laws.

title: Product Manager, eCommerce Solutions
description:
Ready to take your career global?

Make your mark at one of the biggest names in payments. We’re looking for a Product Manager, eCommerce Solutions to join our ever evolving Product team and help shape the future of global commerce. Whether you're a merchant accepting payments, a bank issuing cards or a developer embedding payment technology, if it has anything to do with commerce, we're already on it! That's why 6m+ merchant locations and 7k+ software partners around the world rely on Global Payments to handle more than 94b transactions every year.

In Asia, Global Payments serves the small and medium business segment across Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, Malaysia, Singapore and the Philippines. Our merchants are the retailers, cafes, clinics and online sellers that make up most businesses in these markets. Few employ a payments specialist or a developer, so they rely on us to make acceptance work and to keep them on the right side of rules they had no part in writing.

Our SMB strategy is software-led. We bring payment acceptance together with the point-of-sale and eCommerce software merchants already use, so a small business can scale without first becoming a payments expert.

What you’ll own

  • Own compliance and mandate delivery by tracking card scheme and regulatory changes, translating requirements into product features, managing implementation timelines, and ensuring PCI DSS compliance for eCommerce acceptance.

  • Design seamless compliance solutions for SMBs, delivering requirements through the platform and partner integrations while minimizing effort and disruption for merchants.

  • Drive payment performance and conversion, improving approval rates, reducing false declines and authentication abandonment, and managing fraud and chargeback ratios.

  • Analyze payment data and optimize authorization outcomes, using insights to enhance exemption strategies, token management, credential updates, retry logic, and issuer performance.

  • Act as the compliance and payments subject matter expert, educating stakeholders on scheme changes, advocating for SMB merchant needs, collaborating with global platform teams, and evaluating emerging payment models and industry trends.

What you’ll bring

  • 5+ years of payments product management or delivery experience, with strong expertise in card-not-present (CNP) payment environments.

  • Deep understanding of card scheme mandates and compliance requirements, with the ability to interpret scheme bulletins and assess impacts on platforms and merchant portfolios.

  • Hands-on knowledge of the eCommerce payments ecosystem, including payment gateways, hosted and embedded checkouts, EMV 3DS, tokenization, fraud prevention tools, and alternative payment methods.

  • Proven track record of delivering compliance and regulatory initiatives to fixed deadlines, including experience with authentication, tokenization, fraud monitoring programs, and PCI DSS compliance.

  • Strong technical and operational capabilities, including SMB and partner-led distribution experience, independent stakeholder management, familiarity with REST APIs and basic SQL, and experience working in agile delivery environments.

About the team

Our inclusive and global teams win together every day. We’re proud to have the best minds in the industry, who you can learn from as you grow your career. The people, the energy, the connections – it’s unmatched. Come and be part of an ever-evolving company and get dynamic opportunities that go beyond borders.

What makes a Globalpayer?

Globalpayers think like a client, act like an owner and win as one team. We’re curious and innovative – always finding better ways to deliver impact. We empower each other to make decisions, and it’s our passion that drives excellence in everything we set out to do.

Does this sound like you? Then you sound like a Globalpayer. Apply now to take your career global.

title: Software Engineer - Python/Typescript
description:
About Turing

Turing is one of the world’s leading AGI infrastructure companies, working with frontier AI labs to accelerate model development through high-quality training data, evaluations, and engineering talent.

About the Role

We’re looking for experienced, hands-on software engineers to help evaluate and improve AI coding models.

Rather than primarily building production applications, you’ll work with coding agents across real-world repositories and assess the quality of their work. You’ll review generated code and agent behavior, determine whether solutions are technically correct, identify failure modes, and create the evaluation signals and feedback used to improve model performance.

Think of the coding agent as another engineer whose work you’re reviewing: Can it understand the task? Did it choose the right approach? Is the resulting code correct, robust, and maintainable? Can you explain precisely where it succeeded or failed?

What You’ll Do

  • Evaluate AI-generated code and solutions across real-world software repositories
  • Review agent behavior, tool usage, and code changes for correctness and quality
  • Identify technical errors, weak approaches, and recurring model failure modes
  • Compare model outputs and explain why one solution is better than another
  • Create and refine rubrics and evaluation criteria for coding tasks
  • Produce high-quality evaluation and preference data used to improve coding models
  • Build and maintain pipelines and infrastructure supporting data generation, collection, and evaluation workflows
  • Synthesize findings from data work into clear write-ups, updates, and recommendations for the team
  • Collaborate closely with researchers and engineers to translate qualitative judgment into scalable processes
  • Share clear, actionable findings with AI researchers and engineers

What We’re Looking For

  • 5+ years of hands-on software engineering experience
  • Strong proficiency in Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, or another major production language
  • Experience working in substantial real-world codebases
  • Strong code-review skills and technical judgment
  • Ability to clearly explain why an implementation is correct, incorrect, or could be improved
  • Strong written communication
  • Experience using modern LLMs or AI coding tools
Experience with LLM evaluation, coding agents, RLHF, preference data, rubric design, or post-training is a plus, but not required.

Engagement Details

  • Compensation: Market rate; please provide a specific hourly rate expectation
  • Availability: 40 hours/week preferred, with at least 6 hours of Pacific Time overlap
  • Type: Independent contractor

title: Research Coordinator
description:
Location: This role is based at Output Sports’ office in NovaUCD, Dublin. The successful candidate must be based in, or able to commute regularly to, Dublin.

Coordinate and drive the applied research and product validation work behind Output Sports' performance technology. As Research Coordinator, you will drive the day-to-day delivery of internal and external research across validity, reliability, normative data and applied performance studies in key testing domains including velocity-based training, jump testing, reactive strength index, mobility and balance - and you will make sure that high-quality research and evidence inform our product and reaches the athletes, coaches, customers, partners and organisations who can act on it.

Role Overview

This role sits at the intersection of sports science, biomechanics and product innovation within a fast-growing sports technology company. You will coordinate and execute Output Sports' applied research roadmap, spanning internal and external validity and reliability studies, applied research and other evidence-generation priorities, while also building the external relationships, funding pipeline and research outputs that turn that research into product, commercial and scientific impact.

You will work closely with Output Sports’ internal R&D and product leadership, as well as experienced external academic and research advisors, to ensure that research priorities, methodologies and outputs remain scientifically rigorous and aligned with company priorities. You will also draw on specialist scientific, engineering and commercial expertise as required.

Your Responsibilities


Applied Research, Data Collection & Validation

  • Design, coordinate and execute research protocols evaluating Output Sports IMU performance, validity and reliability across velocity-based training, jump testing, reactive strength index, mobility, balance assessments and other priority testing domains, including applied and use-case research where relevant.
  • Run athlete testing sessions comparing Output Sports outputs against appropriate criterion or reference systems, including force plates and Linear Position Transducers, ensuring accurate setup, calibration, synchronisation and data quality across all measurement systems.
  • Conduct and interpret appropriate statistical analyses for research and validation studies, selecting methods suited to the research question. This may include agreement, reliability and validity analyses such as correlations, ICCs and Bland-Altman analyses.
  • Maintain appropriate research documentation and data-quality processes, including study protocols, data cleaning, version control, analysis records and clear storage of research outputs.

Research Strategy, Governance & Portfolio Management

  • Maintain and help prioritise Output Sports' research roadmap across internal studies, external collaborations and funded research projects.
  • Evaluate inbound research and collaboration opportunities and provide recommendations based on scientific value, strategic fit, required resources and relevance to Output's product and research priorities.
  • Maintain visibility of active and prospective studies, datasets, publications and collaboration opportunities, ensuring key internal stakeholders are kept informed.
  • Coordinate appropriate research governance, including confidentiality, data access, permissions, collaboration documentation, publication rights and IP considerations, escalating specialist legal or technical matters where required.
  • Work with internal stakeholders and external academic advisors to review research priorities, methodology and publication strategy.

Research Collaboration Management

  • Build and manage relationships with university, institute and applied research partners to establish and run joint validation, reliability, applied-performance and product-relevant studies.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for external researchers and collaborators, coordinating research scope and protocols, timelines, formal collaboration documentation, Output technology or research resources, and deliverables.
  • Manage a pipeline of active and prospective research collaborations, keeping internal stakeholders updated on progress and outcomes.

Research Translation & Business Enablement

  • Translate validity, reliability and applied research findings into clear, accurate resources for product, sports science, customer success, sales and marketing, including web content, white papers, one-pagers, technical summaries and sales-support materials.
  • Maintain Output Sports' central research and evidence base, including the research and validation content on the Output Sports research Notion website, ensuring that published findings, validity and reliability evidence and key statistics remain accurate and current.
  • Work with product, marketing, and commercial teams to translate technical results into messaging that is credible to practitioners and compelling to buyers.
  • Support the preparation of internal reports, presentations, and research-led white papers for wider business use.
  • Support the preparation, submission and dissemination of peer-reviewed publications and other scientific outputs, including liaison with collaborators and consideration of appropriate publication routes.

Funding Identification & Application

  • Identify relevant grant, innovation, and research funding opportunities (e.g. Enterprise Ireland, Horizon Europe, academic-industry partnership schemes) aligned with Output Sports' R&D priorities.
  • Coordinate, lead or co-author funding and grant applications in collaboration with academic partners and internal stakeholders.
  • Once funding is secured, support the scoping and delivery of funded research projects, coordinating internal and external stakeholders to ensure the project delivers against Output Sports' research priorities.
  • Track funding deadlines, reporting requirements, and compliance obligations for any secured funding.

Team & Project Leadership

  • Coordinate and maintain the research roadmap, helping to prioritise multiple concurrent validation, applied research and data projects.
  • Help recruit, onboard, supervise and mentor research interns and assistants, planning their work and reviewing testing protocols, data collection, analysis and data quality.
  • Coordinate off-site athlete testing and data-collection activity where required, including participants, equipment and practical research logistics.
  • Work closely with product and engineering teams to feed device performance, usability, and research findings back into the product roadmap.
  • Stay informed on emerging trends in sports science, biomechanics, wearable technology, and performance analytics, and bring relevant developments back into the team.
This role is ideal for someone with a strong academic grounding in sports science, biomechanics or a related discipline and real experience running applied research - someone who is equally comfortable designing and running field or lab-based testing, working with and interpreting data, and representing Output Sports to a university, research partner or funding body. You will lead research design, data collection and analysis, collaboration management, and the translation of findings into content that supports both marketing and the wider business.

Requirements

  • Degree in Sports Science, Biomechanics, Kinesiology, Exercise Physiology, Physiotherapy or a related field. A Master's degree, postgraduate research qualification or equivalent applied research experience is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and running research or validation studies, ideally involving wearable technology, force plates, LPTs, or motion capture systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to clean, analyse and interpret research data, with working proficiency in at least one appropriate statistical analysis environment such as R, Python, SPSS or equivalent.
  • Comfortable undertaking practical athlete testing and occasional off-site data collection or travel where required.
  • Ability to critically evaluate research quality and determine whether findings or proposed studies are sufficiently rigorous and relevant to support Output Sports’ research priorities.
  • Strong understanding of resistance training movements (e.g. squat, bench press, countermovement jump) and velocity-based training principles.
  • Proven ability to manage external relationships and collaborative projects, with strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience translating technical or scientific findings into content for non-specialist audiences.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects, testing sessions, and deadlines.

Desirables

  • Familiarity with Output Sports technology.

  • Experience with source‑code management, automated build pipelines and mobile application release processes.

  • Had experience using artificial intelligence tools to generate, automate or maintain test cases for regression and enhancement testing.
  • Familiarity with Agile software development methodologies is a plus.

  • Strong sense of accountability for application quality, stability and successful delivery.

title: Senior AI Data Engineer, Data Products & RAG Foundations
company: AU00 Agilent Technologies Australia Pty Ltd
description:
About the role:

Agilent helps laboratories around the world advance scientific discovery, diagnostics, and applied market solutions through instruments, software, consumables, services, and deep domain expertise.

As a Senior AI Data Engineer, Data Products & RAG Foundations, you will be a data engineering SME within a cross-functional AI pod, working alongside AI engineers, domain experts, business stakeholders, data owners, and platform teams. Your role is to build data products, pipelines, metadata, and retrieval-ready assets that power AI-enabled business and scientific workflows across the enterprise. Pods do not wait for the enterprise data foundation to be complete; they help build it through execution. Every data product created by the pod is designed for governance, reuse, and long-term value, with the next consumer in mind from day one.

This role goes beyond traditional data engineering. You will work with structured and unstructured data, semantic definitions, quality scoring, lineage, contracts, embeddings, vector search, and retrieval foundations for AI systems. You will also leverage AI-assisted techniques, such as metadata generation, entity resolution, and content classification, to create trusted, AI-ready data products at scale.

You do not need prior experience with Agilent’s internal data architecture. We are looking for a strong data engineer who understands data quality, governance, and AI-ready data foundations and is excited to help shape the future of enterprise AI at Agilent.

What you will do:

  • Build and maintain AI-ready data products and pipelines for the pod's use case, ensuring appropriate governance, lineage, metadata, access controls, and documentation from the start. Design data products for reuse, treating every asset as a potential enterprise capability rather than a point integration.
  • Establish data quality standards, quality scoring, and model-readiness criteria that support reliable AI behavior and business outcomes. Ensure quality issues are identified and addressed before they impact downstream AI solutions.
  • Partner with data owners, stewards, business stakeholders, and IT teams to establish trusted definitions, authoritative sources, and domain data models. Ensure AI solutions are grounded in validated business meaning rather than convenience-based access to data.
  • Design retrieval foundations that support AI applications, including structured and unstructured grounding, vector search, graph-based approaches, and semantic enrichment where appropriate.
  • Apply AI-assisted techniques such as metadata generation, entity resolution, and content classification to improve the quality, scalability, and discoverability of data assets.
  • Design and implement scalable ingestion, integration, and storage frameworks across cloud and on-premises environments. Build reusable data assets, tools, and services that support AI engineers, data scientists, and analytics teams. Contribute reusable data products, patterns, and documentation back to the broader enterprise ecosystem.

What success looks like in the first year:

  • The pod's use case is running entirely on governed, quality-scored data products, with no undocumented or unsupported data sources.
  • Multiple data products created by the pod have been adopted, reused, or identified for reuse across additional AI or analytics use cases.
  • Data quality signals are integrated into AI evaluation and monitoring processes, influencing AI behavior and outcomes.
  • Data-to-build time has measurably improved through reuse, automation, and process optimization.

Qualifications

  • Technical Expertise – Strong data engineering experience building AI-ready data products, not just warehouse tables and dashboards.
  • Hands-on familiarity – with platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake, vector databases, graph stores, and operating under data contracts, lineage, and certification requirements.
  • Experience – with RAG foundations, including chunking, embedding, hybrid retrieval, and understanding how retrieval quality impacts agent/ AI behavior and outcomes.
  • Domain and Product Mindset – A disposition to work within a business domain, partnering with data stewards and subject matter experts to understand the meaning behind the data. An instinct to build for reuse, creating assets intended for second consumers and use cases, not just the first.
  • Communication and Influence – Excellent communication and the ability to influence technical and non-technical audiences. Able to build trusted partnerships with domain experts, stewards, business stakeholders and functions such as Legal, Quality, and Security.
  • Curiosity and Growth Mindset – Curiosity about AI, its opportunities, limitations, staying informed about emerging approaches, while maintaining a healthy skepticism and focus on responsible implementation. A lifelong learner who continuously adapts skills and ways of working in a rapidly evolving field.
  • Education and Seniority – Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Data Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Typically, at least 8+ years of relevant experience for entry to this level.

Additional Details

  • This job has a full time weekly schedule.
  • Our pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. During the hiring process, a recruiter can share more about the specific pay range for a preferred location.

title: Information Scientist (Applied Technology Policy)
description:
Job Type:

Regular

Position Description

Are you passionate about using your analytical skills to address critical policy challenges? RAND is seeking talented Information Scientists to join our team and contribute to impactful research in national security policy.

RAND researchers contribute to and lead innovative projects that deliver objective, reliable insights for the public and policymakers at multiple levels. They embrace challenges on diverse topics that require strong analytic capabilities, technical knowledge, and academic, industry, or government experience in organizational processes and decision-making.

Why RAND?

· Reputation for Excellence: Be part of a non-profit, non-partisan organization renowned for its rigorous and objective research.

· Dynamic Opportunities: Collaborate in multidisciplinary teams on diverse projects that challenge and expand your skills.

· Poised for Impact: Your research will inform thousands of policymakers, clients, and other stakeholders around the world.

Responsibilities:

Information Scientists at RAND apply their analytical and technical expertise to:

  • Examine complex policy problems by developing innovative research approaches such as modeling and simulation and novel artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tools.

  • Execute this research using a broad range of analytically rigorous quantitative and qualitative research tools, methods, and skills.

  • Interpret research results to support stakeholder decision-making.

  • Communicate research results to policymakers and the public at all levels through written products and oral presentations.

  • Contribute to business development efforts

Qualifications

Successful applicants will have demonstrated technical or methodological skills, and/or domain knowledge in the technical design, development, testing, application, and/or operation of information, communications, space, automation, or AI/machine learning systems. Relevant skills and knowledge may include:

  • Cybersecurity systems implementation, security assurance, vulnerability risk management, or adversarial testing of AI-enabled systems

  • Development, deployment, and evaluation of AI-enabled research or decision-support tools, including LLM applications, agentic workflows, or human-in-the-loop analytical systems

  • Development, application, or policy analysis of financial technology systems, including digital assets and technology-enabled financial platforms and services

  • Development of modeling and simulation approaches for space, autonomous, robotic, or other complex systems

  • Analysis of large, complex datasets using data science or machine-learning methods


All research positions at RAND require excellent analytic skills; the ability to communicate clearly and effectively in English, both orally and in writing; the ability to work effectively as a member of a multi-disciplinary team; and a strong commitment to RAND's core values of quality and objectivity.

Experience

Experience with components of the Department of War is highly desired.

Professional or academic experience with a focus on the technical design, development, testing, application, and/or operation of engineered systems are preferred.

Successful applicants will be able to present strong evidence of research experience, demonstrated through authorship of academic publications, conference presentations, or prior professional reports. They will also be versatile with multiple research methods.

Education Requirements

A PhD, MS, or BS in computer science or engineering, information science, cyberengineering, robotics, or related field (such as mathematics, operations research, physical sciences, or closely related discipline) is required. A PhD with at least 2 years of relevant professional experience is preferred. Applicants with a masters degree must have at least 5 years of professional experience; applicants with a bachelors degree must have at least 10 years of professional experience. Professional experience should demonstrate the applicant’s ability to design, execute and disseminate results of research using analytically rigorous methods.

Security Clearance

Candidates must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance. Please note that U.S. citizenship is required to obtain and maintain a government security clearance. Candidates with an active U.S. security clearance are preferred.

Location

Washington, DC; Santa Monica, CA; Pittsburgh PA

Writing Sample Required

Successful applications will include documentation in the application package of academic and professional activities that meet stated qualifications. A writing sample of 3 pages or more is required when applying for this position. Applicants are encouraged to use recent research published in academic journals, conference proceedings, or research reports but may use reports or papers written for prior employment. Applicants whose written products have dissemination restrictions (e.g., are classified), may submit a short, written summary (i.e., less than one page) of one or more recent products they have developed. Note that applicants invited to interview will be required to provide a writing sample and present a seminar describing recent research. Writing samples can be redacted or subsequently submitted through restricted channels and the seminar can be held in a classified environment as needed.

Salary Range: $108,000 - $215,400

Associate Researcher: $108,000 - $174,000

Full Researcher: $123,100 - $215,400

Title: Director, Highway Operations

Department: Highway Operations

Location: 6200 Steeles Ave West, Woodbridge

Position Summary:

The Director, Operations is an on-site leadership role based at 407 ETR's Woodbridge office providing strategic and operational leadership for the maintenance, safety, incident response, winter operations, tolling operations, and contractor management activities across Highway 407 ETR. The role is accountable for ensuring operations are delivered safely, efficiently, and cost-effectively while maintaining compliance with the Concession and Ground Lease Agreement (CGLA), applicable legislation, regulatory requirements, and corporate objectives.

The Director, Operations oversees operational planning, resource management, emergency preparedness, contractor performance, continuous improvement initiatives, and the development of high-performing teams. The role requires a visible field presence during critical events and operational activities to provide leadership, support effective decision-making, and ensure a coordinated response.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Provide strategic leadership, technical guidance, and operational oversight for all highway maintenance, patrol, and tolling operations, ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with operational requirements.

  • Establish and oversee the Safety Control Plan, ensuring compliance with the Concession and Ground Lease Agreement, applicable legislation, industry standards, and corporate safety objectives.

  • Lead the development and presentation of operational performance reporting, providing insights on key achievements, service levels, operational effectiveness, and cost performance to support executive decision-making

  • Serve as the primary Operations representative for internal, external, and regulatory audits, ensuring compliance with applicable legislation, contractual obligations, and corporate governance requirements.

  • Provide strategic leadership in the development and execution of annual Operating and Capital budgets, establishing priorities, allocating resources, and ensuring expenditures align with business objectives and operational requirements.

  • Direct the planning, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Summer and Winter Operations Programs, ensuring operational readiness, resource optimization, regulatory compliance, and effective deployment of personnel, fleet,and materials to maintain safe roadway conditions and tolling technology.

  • Establish governance and oversight for work activity permits, lane closure approvals, and traffic management activities, balancing operational, maintenance, construction, customer, and safety requirements.

  • Oversee the resolution of complex customer concerns and operational issues, ensuring timely responses, continuous improvement, and protection of the organization's reputation.

  • Represent the organization in legal proceedings, discoveries, claims, and litigation matters related to highway operations, providing subject matter expertise and operational leadership.

  • Provide leadership during major incidents, emergencies, and business continuity events, ensuring effective coordination of resources, stakeholder communications, and timely resolution of operational impacts.

  • Develop and maintain strategic partnerships with government agencies, regulatory bodies, law enforcement, municipalities, industry associations, and external stakeholders, advancing organizational objectives and supporting the safe and effective operation of highway infrastructure.

  • Administer and oversee vendor contracts, including tender development, contract negotiations, amendments, extensions, performance monitoring, and ensuring contractual provisions protect the corporation's interests.

  • Oversee fleet lifecycle management, including maintenance, replacement planning, technical specifications, and evaluation of new technologies, pilot programs, and operational equipment improvements.

Qualifications:

  • University degree in Civil Engineering, Transportation Engineering, or a related discipline. An equivalent combination of education and extensive operational leadership experience may be considered.

  • Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in highway operations, infrastructure maintenance, transportation, construction, or a related field, including significant experience in a senior leadership role.

  • Extensive knowledge of freeway operations, maintenance standards, safety regulations, and legislative requirements governing high-volume urban freeway environments.

  • Demonstrated success leading large, multidisciplinary teams and developing high-performing leaders within a complex operational environment.

  • Strong business and financial acumen, including experience managing operational budgets, resource planning, vendor relationships, and performance metrics.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and operational management systems, including asset management, maintenance management, and reporting platforms.

  • Exceptional judgment, strategic thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make sound decisions in complex and time-sensitive situations.

  • Outstanding communication, interpersonal, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to effectively engage executives, government agencies, emergency services, contractors, and customers.

  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to operational excellence, regulatory compliance, accuracy, and continuous improvement.

  • Proven planning and organizational skills, with the ability to establish priorities, manage competing demands, and execute long-term operational strategies.

  • Demonstrated ability to perform effectively in high-pressure environments, including emergency response and critical incident management.

  • Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion, professionalism, and integrity.

  • Valid driver's license and ability to respond to operational requirements as needed.

We are actively seeking to fill this role as it is a current vacancy.

Highway 407 ETR is an all-electronic open-access toll highway located in the Greater Toronto Area in Ontario, Canada. The highway spans 108 kilometres from Burlington in the west to Pickering in the east.

Job Description

This role is critical in ensuring a successful post-merger integration by bridging strategy and execution across applications, infrastructure, cybersecurity, data, and operational processes. The ideal candidate is a seasoned technology leader with experience leading complex enterprise technology integrations transformations, Day 1 readiness activities and target operating model build-outs post-merger.

The Technology Leader will serve as a key member of the Integration Management Office (IMO), responsible for leading the technology integration workstream. This technology role will develop and execute comprehensive integration strategies across IT systems, applications, infrastructure, cybersecurity, data, service management, and end-user technologies to ensure seamless business continuity from Day 1 through long-term transformation.

The successful candidate will partner closely with business leaders, functional integration teams, technology stakeholders, and external partners to define integration priorities, manage risks, drive execution, and enable the realization of synergies and business value.

Key Responsibilities

Integration Strategy & Planning

  • Develop and lead the IT integration strategy aligned with transaction objectives, synergy targets, and business priorities.
  • Establish and manage the technology integration roadmap, including Day 1, Day 100, and longer-term integration milestones.
  • Conduct technology due diligence assessments and evaluate systems, platforms, infrastructure, cybersecurity posture, and support models.
  • Support the definition of future-state architecture and operating model for the combined organization.
  • Identify integration risks, dependencies, critical decisions, and mitigation plans.

Integration Management Office Leadership

  • Represent the technology function within the Technology Integration Management Office (TIMO).
  • Facilitate technology integration workstreams and coordinate activities across multiple functional and business teams.
  • Develop detailed work plans, milestones, dependencies, resourcing requirements, and governance processes.
  • Provide senior leadership level status reporting, issue escalation, and decision support to integration leadership and steering committees.
  • Drive cross-functional alignment to ensure integration objectives are achieved on schedule and within budget.

Technology Integration Execution

  • Facilitate the integration of enterprise applications, infrastructure, cloud environments, networks, collaboration platforms, end-user computing, and operational technology.
  • Guide the functional leaders through the data migration, application rationalization, platform consolidation, and technology modernization initiatives.
  • Support business continuity and operational stability during all phases of integration.
  • Coordinate vendor, partner, and third-party technology integration activities and communications.

Cybersecurity, Risk & Compliance

  • Support the functional leads in evaluating cybersecurity risks and develop integration plans that maintain security and regulatory compliance.
  • Ensure alignment with corporate governance, data privacy, regulatory, audit, and compliance requirements.

Organizational Readiness & Change Management

  • Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration, and execution excellence across integration teams.
  • Partner with business and HR leaders to support organizational readiness, communication, and change management efforts.
  • Prepare technology teams and end users for Day 1 operational readiness.
  • Help establish support structures, service management capabilities, and transition plans for the combined organization.

Value Realization

  • Identify and drive technology-related synergy opportunities, cost optimization initiatives, and operational efficiencies.
  • Track and report realization of integration benefits and business outcomes.
  • Ensure technology integration decisions support strategic growth, scalability, and long-term value creation.

Qualifications

Required Experience

The Department of Finance of The Pennsylvania State University (University Park) seeks to fill up to three tenure-line faculty positions, including two Assistant Professors and one Full Professor position, beginning in Fall 2027. In particular, candidates must conduct high-quality research that is published or publishable in top-tier academic journals; effectively teach at the undergraduate and graduate levels; serve as a research advisor and mentor to PhD students; engage in service activities commensurate with their rank; and contribute to the collegial and intellectual atmosphere of the department.

Those who are in the final stages of completing a PhD program will be considered for appointments as an Assistant Professor. Candidates for all ranks must have a PhD in Finance or a closely related field by the appointment start date.

APPLICATION PROCEDURE:

  • copies of representative publications and working papers

A minimum of three reference letters should be emailed directly from reference providers to this address: finance.recruiting@psu.edu

title: Hiring: Developer - Front End Web
description:
Role:

We are looking for an experienced, highly motivated Python developer with expertise in building robust data pipelines, creating and manipulating DataFrames, and turning defined specifications into reliable, production grade scripts. The role centres on developing and orchestrating the data infrastructure behind a systematic research platform: document analysis engines that extract structured data from financial filings and disclosures, integrated with market and transaction datasets into a point in time research database. This is a genuine opportunity to extend into quantitative research and to help build the foundation for full stack, next gen SaaS service offerings.

Key Responsibilities:
• Bulletproof script development: build reliable, production grade scripts from defined specifications.
• Data orchestration and integration: develop and own the orchestration scripts that integrate multiple data feeds (document analysis output, transaction data, market data) into the existing point in time database on a reliable schedule, continuously improving the dataset's quality and coverage.
• Document analysis engines: develop and improve engines that turn financial filings and disclosures into structured, queryable data, including LLM assisted extraction where appropriate.
• Testing to production migration: own the path from development to production, testing rigorously in a staging environment before migrating scripts to the production server with proper versioning, rollback capability and zero disruption to live processes.
• Data hygiene, processing and transformation: apply disciplined data hygiene across sources, including deduplication, entity and identifier mapping, and handling of missing or malformed values, with close attention to point in time integrity (as of date versioning, no look ahead bias, clean handling of revisions).
• Automation and optimisation: automate data workflows and build in data quality checks so parsing failures, gaps or stale data are caught before they reach research.
• Documentation and code quality: write well documented, maintainable code with unit tests covering data processing and integration scripts. Clear, thorough documentation of what's built, how it works and how to run it is a core part of the role, so work can be understood, maintained and handed over by others.
• Foundation development: contribute to backend API development, user authentication and database integration, laying groundwork for a scalable SaaS platform.
• Any other ad hoc duties that may be required from time to time

Technical Requirements:
• Proven experience with Python, especially Pandas and NumPy
• Mastery of SQL and PostgreSQL: schema design, complex queries, indexing and performance optimisation, beyond basic querying
• Experience with pipeline orchestration and scheduling
• Proven ability to deliver reliable, tested scripts against a written specification, and to migrate them cleanly from a test environment to a production server
• Strong data hygiene, processing and cleaning skills, including experience with messy real world data (documents, filings, PDFs, HTML, third party APIs)
• A habit of documenting your own work thoroughly, so others can understand, maintain and build on it
• LLM API experience for structured data extraction, and general comfort working with AI tools and prompting.
• An understanding of point in time data is a strong plus

Also desirable: experience with vector databases (pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant or similar); machine learning experience (PyTorch, TensorFlow, XGBoost/LightGBM) for building, maintaining and extending existing models; Bloomberg API integration to Python; data science/statistics, signal research, backtesting or factor modelling; full stack familiarity (Flask, Django, FastAPI); SaaS build/deploy on cloud (Docker, AWS or similar); an understanding of Java; and experience in quantitative finance or with financial market data.

Qualifications & Experience:
• Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science, Data Science, IT, Electrical Engineering or equivalent experience is essential
• Experience working in a regulated financial services industry, preferable but not essential
• Proactive approach towards identifying opportunities for improvement and taking ownership to deliver solutions

title: Psychiatrist - Migration Field (On-Call Work)
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration


Project Context and Scope

Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission, the direct supervision of the Migration and Health Physician, the successful candidate shall be responsible for providing medical examination for beneficiaries, technical and operational oversight for the Mission’s migration health portfolio,) as needed. Their primary responsibility will be to provide psychiatric assessments, interventions, and support to migrants, work closely with a multidisciplinary team to address the mental health needs and ensure the well-being of individuals and families.


Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing

In close ccordination with MHD and MHPPS teams with clear elaborated referral mechanism and case management.
Tasks to be performed under this contract
  • Psychiatric Assessments: Conduct psychiatric assessments and screenings for migrants upon their arrival. Evaluate and document their mental health conditions, identify any immediate psychiatric concerns, and provide necessary follow-up, care.

  • Crisis Intervention: Respond to psychiatric crises and provide immediate psychiatric care to migrants in acute distress. This includes conducting risk assessments, crisis management, and providing therapeutic interventions to stabilize patients.

  • Mental Health Support: Offer individual and group therapy sessions to migrants, addressing a range of mental health issues such as trauma, anxiety, depression, and adjustment difficulties. Provide psychoeducational on coping strategies and resilience-building techniques.
    Collaborative Care: Collaborate with the multidisciplinary team to develop individualized care plans for migrants with complex mental health needs. Coordinate with other healthcare providers, social workers, and interpreters to ensure holistic and culturally sensitive care.

  • Capacity Building and Training: Provide training and support to healthcare staff, including nurses and social workers, on recognizing and addressing common mental health issues among migrants. Offer guidance on best practices for promoting positive mental health.

  • Documentation and Reporting: Maintain accurate and up-to-date medical records, documenting psychiatric assessments, treatments, and follow-up care provided to migrants. Prepare regular reports on psychiatric activities and outcomes for internal and external reporting purposes.

  • On-Call Work: Be available for on-call shifts, as needed, to provide urgent psychiatric consultations and interventions for migrants experiencing mental health emergencies outside of regular working hours.

  • Perform any other duties as may be assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Medical degree with specialization in Psychiatry and valid license to practice psychiatry in the relevant jurisdiction.

Experience

  • Experience working in the field of migration health, refugee mental health, or a similar healthcare setting is preferred.

  • Knowledge of trauma-informed care, cultural psychiatry, and cross-cultural communication techniques.

  • Empathy, cultural sensitivity, and the ability to build rapport with individuals from diverse cultural backgrounds.

  • Strong clinical assessment and diagnostic skills, with the ability to formulate appropriate treatment plans.

  • Ability to work in a fast-paced and high-pressure environment, demonstrating resilience.

Languages

  • Fluency in English and French (oral and written).

  • Working knowledge of Arabic is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

title: Advd Practice Clinician PRN
description:

Job Summary:

The Advanced Practice Clinician (NP/PA) is service/physician aligned, managing a distinct patient population. The APC may be required to perform some outpatient and inpatient care and facilitate discharges/outpatient follow up. The APC has a strong foundation in evidenced based practice/education and is responsible for ensuring adherence to clinical pathways/protocols and ensures an environment of safe quality care. The APC demonstrates advanced level of medical and nursing knowledge, clinical/technical competence, sound clinical judgement, professional communication skills, timely and compliant documentation, and responsible for professional development and competency validation.

.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • The APC may serve as the first responder for both nursing and staff in the event of patient status changes, orders, and in situations requiring procedural and resuscitative interventions.
  • Assesses for risks associated with the care of the acute and complex chronically ill patient including medication side effects, immobility, impaired nutrition, fluid, and electrolyte imbalance, immunocompetence, invasive interventions and diagnostic procedures.
  • Coordinates daily clinic schedule with the attending physician team, presents patient report, collaborates in plan of care, and follows assigned patient population.
  • Manages diagnostic tests through ordering, inter
  • Formulates Plan of Care

  • Utilizes evidenced based practice guidelines or protocols in an individualized, dynamic plan of care that can be applied across the continuum.
  • Implements and modifies plan of care
  • Prescribes diagnostic strategies and therapeutic interventions both pharmacologic, non-pharmacologic, and surgical, needed to achieve expected outcomes.
  • Manages further diagnostic tests through ordering, interpretation, performance, and supervision.
  • May perform advanced procedures consistent with privileges and competency validation, including minor suturing, complex wound management, line and tube placements and removals
  • Communication and Collaboration
  • Maintains ongoing communication and collaboration with interdisciplinary health care team.
  • Facilitates and communicates with patient, family, and staff to promote c
  • Documentation

(h&p, daily progress notes, plan of care, problem lists, procedure notes, acute event note, discharge summaries in medical record per specific patient unit or service, death mmary)
  • Documentation is timely, meets critical care compliance standards and captures patient acuity.
  • Professional Practice
  • Demonstrates Professional Practice behaviors including preceptor/mentoring, education and instruction of students, nursing staff, nurses, graduate, and novice APCs
  • Seeks opportunities for active engagement in research and the analysis of evidenced based practice.
  • Actively participates in Grand Rounds, APN council meetings, faculty and unit meetings, M&M presentations.
  • Maintains CEUs, and membership in a professional organization.

title: Academic Advisor II
description:
Job Title

Academic Advisor II

Agency

Texas A&M University - Corpus Christi

Department

Academic Advising

Proposed Minimum Salary

Commensurate

Job Location

Corpus Christi, Texas

Job Type

Staff

Job Description

TAMU-CC is a dynamic university designated as both a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) and Minority-Serving Institution (MSI) with approximately 11,000 students from 47 states and 54 foreign nations. We employ over 1,400 full-time and 2,000 part-time Islanders (including students/GAs). The University attracts highly talented faculty and staff and offers an array of undergraduate and graduate degrees, including doctoral programs. As a member of the Texas A&M University System, TAMU-CC benefits from a range of resources, increased visibility and influence, and opportunities to collaborate in mutually beneficial ways with peers across member institutions and associated agencies.

TAMU-CC’s beautiful campus is located on a 240-acre island on Corpus Christi Bay and was ranked #1 College by the Sea by Best College Reviews. Our natural setting is enhanced by its modern, attractive, and state-of-the-art classroom buildings and support facilities.

PURPOSE

This position under general supervision, advises students concerning the academic requirements for their chosen program and reports directly to the Senior Academic Advisor. This position is responsible for assisting students with course selection, registration process, and major selection. This position provides information on and refers students to university resources that can assist in meeting their needs or solving problems; communicates accurate and timely information and interprets institutional, core, and major requirements. May supervise projects.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Academic Advising: 65%

  • Provides academic advising for students grounded in tenets of practice outlined by the National Association of Academic Advising (NACADA) and appropriate academic advising and student development theories.

  • Advises for course selection, registration, academic planning, career and educational goal-setting, appropriate resources, transitioning to the university, and retention issues. Document student advising outcomes adequately to meet department and institutional disclosure guidelines and aid in subsequent advising activities.

  • Advises in both group and individual settings with current and prospective students.

  • Perform appointment preparations including, but not limited to, reviewing all accessible academic records for accuracy and appropriateness of course work, communicating with academic departments for major-specific transfer equivalencies, and requesting the posting of approved transfer courses.

  • Process academic forms and follow-up on processed forms to ensure that the student's record accurately represents the student's chosen major, minor, concentration, and catalog year.

  • Interprets State, University, and college policies and procedures.

  • Complies with all state, system, and university policies, regulations, rules, procedures, guidelines, and directives in a timely manner and adhere to confidentiality policies (FERPA).

Student Success & Retention: 20%

  • Advocate for student needs associated with their educational and academic program. Clearly communicate accurate and timely information to students and interpret institutional, general education, and major requirements per the university catalog. Exhibit strong, active listening skills. Help students develop a realistic self-perception and successful transition into the university and help them to establish realistic goals for future endeavors.

  • Monitors academic progress and implements intervention strategies for students who receive academic alerts or who need assistance in maintaining or improving their academic standing.

  • Direct students to resources, programs and services on campus when it is appropriate to do so. Help students integrate information so that they may make well-informed academic decisions. Work to establish a partnership with students that will guide them efficiently through their academic program.

  • Monitor students advising requirements: Notify students of academic advising requirements when certain conditions have or have not been met. Maintain accurate and complete student file documentation. Prepare for and participate in on- and off-campus recruiting activities. Prepare for, present and advise at first-year student orientations.

  • Support retention efforts include using Navigate and requiring probationary and returning suspension/enforce withdrawal students to schedule an appointment and discuss university guidelines and expectations.

  • Leads workshops, seminars, and other student engagement activities across campus.

  • Leads and oversees special projects specific to the academic college or advising center.

  • Maintain a professional and cordial liaison with administrators, faculty, staff, students, and other involved constituents concerning advisees and program. Track and obtain documents needed for potential and current students from other constituencies on campus.

Collaboration: 10%

  • Collaborates with members of the campus community in student retention initiatives.

  • Seeks opportunities to serve and contribute on appropriate committees and task forces across campus to advocate for students.

  • Conducts research on topics within the field of academic advising and organizes activities for professional development.

  • Attend TAMU-CC Commencement ceremonies.

Reporting/Other: 5%

  • May provide reports and data analysis of advising initiatives and special populations.

  • Mentors and builds strong relationships with other advisors.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree.

  • Two (2) years of experience advising students in higher education or related experience.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, & ABILITIES

  • May travel to national and/or regional advising conferences; may be required to work beyond normal office hours including evening and/or on weekends.

  • Intermediate skills in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook), databases, and spreadsheets.

  • Strong active listening, written, and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability and willingness to work as a team member and to work independently.

  • Demonstrated initiative and follow-through skills; tact, diplomacy, and judgment in dealing with students, parents, faculty, and administrators.

  • Detail-oriented and demonstrated ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment.

  • Ability to work beyond normal office hours including evening and/or weekends.

  • Ability to lead students in developing a sense of purpose and belonging while developing their educational and personal goals.

  • Attend and/or present at the national conference (i.e., NACADA, TEXANN, Texas Success Conference, etc.) and implemented applicable best practices across the unit

  • Ability to use student information systems, degree planning, and degree audits.

  • Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others, present information clearly and concisely, work with sensitive information and maintain confidentiality.

  • Proficient analytical, interpersonal, and organizational skills.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Three (3) years of experience advising students in higher education.

  • Experience with Banner, Argos, Navigate 360, Laserfiche, and Degree Works.

  • Demonstrated knowledge of developmental academic advising methodologies.

SALARY: $3,657.34 Monthly ($43,888.08 Annual, Approximately)

NOTE: Employment may be impacted by the Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025 and the moratorium issued by Texas Governor Abbott on January 27, 2026.

From our generous benefits package and professional development opportunities, to our retirement programs and our commitment to service excellence, the Island University is an engaging and rewarding place to work.
