title: Senior Director, Quality
description:
You may not know our name, but you know our products. What we make is part the places where we live, work and play – all day, everyday.

Zekelman is a family of companies — 100% domestic manufacturers — with a legacy dating back to 1877. We’re proud to be the largest independent steel pipe and tube manufacturer in North America and the leading innovator in multi-family housing development.

We believe in what we build and what we build, builds the world around us. Hospitals, hotels, schools, bridges, airports and more.

Come build a career you believe in.

As Senior Director of Quality at Z Modular, a division of Zekelman Industries, you will establish and lead an independent enterprise Quality organization and Quality Management System across modular manufacturing and construction-related operations. This role sets the strategy, governance, standards, and performance expectations that connect Quality across the full lifecycle, from design and procurement through manufacturing, project delivery, commissioning, turnover, warranty, and asset acceptance.

You will initially lead the Killeen and Chandler plant Quality organizations, assess current people, processes, technology, and controls, and define the future enterprise Quality model. You will partner closely with executive, operational, engineering, supply chain, construction, commissioning, and asset management leaders while maintaining clear, independent Quality authority.

This is a full-time, location-based role near Austin/Killeen, Texas or Phoenix/Chandler, Arizona, requiring 80% or more presence at a Z Modular location. Regular travel between manufacturing facilities and periodic travel to project sites, suppliers, customers, and other business locations is required.

This role is ideal for a practical, experienced manufacturing Quality leader who can build scalable systems, strengthen accountability, influence across functions, and translate complex quality requirements into disciplined operating practices without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.
What You’ll Do
Enterprise Quality Leadership

  • Develop and lead the enterprise Quality strategy, policy direction, objectives, standards architecture, governance model, and maturity roadmap.

  • Advise executive leadership on Quality risk, customer and regulatory exposure, organization capability, technology needs, and investment priorities.

  • Build a culture in which quality is owned at the source, verified objectively, and improved systematically.

  • Lead the enterprise Quality organization and establish clear accountability, role boundaries, development expectations, and succession depth.

  • Establish the enterprise approach for Field QA/QC, including project Quality planning, inspection and test requirements, quality gates, acceptance criteria, nonconformance management, commissioning and turnover readiness, and field-to-manufacturing feedback.

  • Evaluate the future Field/Project Quality organization and determine the resources, qualifications, reporting relationships, and project-specific capabilities required as Z Modular expands third-party work.

Quality Management System and Assurance

  • Establish the direction and minimum requirements for the enterprise Quality Management System, including controlled documentation, records, training governance, audits, management review, nonconformance, CAPA, root cause, change control, and effectiveness verification.

  • Lead ISO 9001 alignment and certification-readiness decisions based on business need, customer expectations, and organizational maturity.

  • Approve the audit and assurance strategy, review systemic trends and significant findings, and ensure corrective actions address causes and prevent recurrence.

  • Define enterprise Quality metrics, calculation principles, thresholds, and reporting expectations; validate data quality before setting performance targets.

Manufacturing and Lifecycle Quality

  • Provide leadership oversight to the Killeen and Chandler Manufacturing Quality teams during the transition and establish consistent expectations for inspections, tests, nonconformance, records, release, and escalation.

  • Partner with Design & Engineering, Procurement, Manufacturing, Logistics, Construction, Commissioning, Turnover, and Asset Management to define lifecycle controls and handoff requirements.

  • Establish a risk-based approach to supplier, product, process, field, commissioning, turnover, and warranty Quality.

  • Ensure customer, contract, code, regulatory, and technical requirements are translated into practical quality plans, inspection and test requirements, evidence, and acceptance criteria.

Organization and Capability Building

  • Assess existing Quality roles, capabilities, workloads, and reporting relationships before finalizing the organization.

  • Validate and fill the required Director, Quality Integration & Continuous Improvement role to lead cross-functional integration, plant Quality operations, process improvement, and lessons learned.

  • Confirm the scope, timing, and staffing for the Manager, Quality Systems & Assurance capability and any future field, supplier, project, audit, data, or specialist roles.

  • Coach Quality leaders and functional partners to strengthen technical judgment, independence, collaboration, and accountability.

Decision Rights, Risk, and External Relationships

  • Establish and maintain defined authority for Quality holds, releases, conditional releases, deviations, waivers, audit escalation, and significant nonconformance.

  • Preserve technical approval authority with the appropriate engineering or operational owner while ensuring Quality requirements, evidence, and risk approvals are complete.

  • Serve as the senior Quality contact for customers, auditors, regulators, third-party inspection agencies, suppliers, and other external stakeholders.

  • Escalate significant regulatory, customer, structural, life-safety, product integrity, or systemic Quality risks to the appropriate executive level.

Technology and Continuous Improvement

  • Evaluate current Quality technology, data flows, module/product traceability, records, dashboards, and integration needs before selecting or expanding solutions.

  • Define business and governance requirements for Quality systems; partner with Enterprise Business Enablement and Information Technology on workflow, reporting, integration, automation, and adoption.

  • Drive improvements that reduce defects, rework, scrap, field corrections, warranty recurrence, delays, and other costs of poor quality.

  • Ensure lessons learned result in updated standards, training, design rules, supplier controls, work instructions, and verification practices.

Who You Are

  • Ten or more years of progressive Quality leadership experience, including substantial experience in complex manufacturing environments.

  • Demonstrated success building, transforming, or materially improving a Quality organization or Quality Management System, rather than only maintaining an established program.

  • Experience leading multi-site or cross-functional Quality teams and partnering with engineering, operations, supply chain, field, customer, and executive stakeholders.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality Management, Manufacturing, Operations, Construction Management, or a related field preferred; an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience may be considered.

  • Hands-on knowledge of ISO 9001 principles, implementation or certification readiness, internal and external audits, management review, controlled documentation, nonconformance, CAPA, root cause, and Quality metrics.

  • Experience with manufacturing Quality, supplier Quality, inspection and testing, product release, warranty and recurrence analysis, and continuous improvement.

  • Ability to establish independent Quality authority while maintaining productive relationships with operational and technical teams.

  • Strong organizational design, people leadership, coaching, influence, change management, executive communication, analytical, and evidence-based decision-making skills.

  • Experience in automotive, industrial equipment, electrical equipment, building products, off-site manufacturing, modular construction, mission-critical projects, or another disciplined production environment preferred.

  • ISO 9001 auditor or implementation training, ASQ credentials, Lean or Six Sigma certification, or relevant construction, welding, inspection, electrical, manufacturing, or regulatory credentials preferred.

  • Ability to work regularly in manufacturing, office, supplier, and active job-site environments and use required personal protective equipment.

  • Eligible to work in the United States.

What You’ll Get

Zekelman Industries offers competitive compensation and excellent benefits, including low-cost, high-quality medical and dental benefits. In addition, we have an amazing tuition assistance program, a bonus plan, a 401(k) plan with a generous company match, loyalty awards, and much more:

title: Senior Investigations Officer
description:
Main Purpose

The Senior Investigations Officer will report to the Global Head of Investigations. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in forensic accounting, investigations, and risk management. The successful individual will work closely with a wide range of departments to identify and investigate Code of Conduct non-compliance and serious misconduct related risks in order to ensure the integrity and security of the organization’s operations. The investigations officer will also work closely with the Operational Risk and Internal Controls team (“ORIC”) to remediate investigation findings and strengthen the control environment.

The remit of the role will include, but not be limited to:

  • Driving excellence - Supporting the Head of Investigations in driving forward an internal investigations team that seeks continued respect and trust from the business, and that is renowned for its professional, timely, proportionate and independent work.

  • Investigation leadership - The oversight and management of substantial / reputationally significant internal investigations across the global business.

  • Leadership - Acting as technical Subject Matter Expert and line manager to the existing Investigations Officers

  • Cross-function collaboration and coordination - Supporting the Head of Investigations / ORIC to create a more connected and collaborative wider team whose combined remit is the design and testing of Internal controls, providing support to the business to strengthen the process and control environment, and to investigate and remediate control, policy and code of conduct breaches.

  • Methodology development - Supporting in the creation and roll-out of robust and consistent investigation and review methodologies, tools and deliverables across the Group.

  • Upskilling in the field of investigations - Developing and providing technical training across the business.

  • Governance support - Providing ad hoc input on initiatives owned by the Risk and Compliance teams that intersect with Fraud / investigations.

  • Issue remediation and anti-fraud framework development - Working with Internal Controls to develop enhanced, dedicated, controls to prevent and detect internal and external fraud; and working with Internal Audit to help establish audit prioritisation based upon the outcome and learnings from investigations.

Key responsibilities

  • To support the Trafigura Global Head of Investigations in addressing the main objectives of the Investigation team (and potentially also across Operational Risk and Internal Control), now and into the future as the objectives and priorities evolve.

  • Under the direction of the Head of Investigations, lead / conduct complex investigations into suspected cases of internal and / or external fraud, financial misconduct, policy non-compliance and other serious cases of misconduct in the context of the Code of Conduct.

  • Interview witnesses and investigation subjects; gather statements, and document findings comprehensively.

  • Prepare/draft detailed investigative reports, including findings, conclusions, and recommendations for review by senior stakeholders within the business. Present investigation results to compliance, senior management and legal counsel as required.

  • Maintain thorough and accurate records of all investigations and related activities.

  • Support the Head of Investigations and ORIC in prioritizing team resource, in supervising ongoing activity and in preparing for reporting required at Board sub-committees and the quarterly Governance and Controls Steering Committee.

  • Contribute to the development and implementation of a risk-based country / market review strategy with supporting investigation plans.

  • Contribute to the design and implementation of anti-fraud strategies, policies, and procedures. Conduct fraud risk assessments and recommend control improvements.

  • Utilize data analytics and forensic tools to detect anomalies and potential fraud indicators.

  • Work closely with internal departments, including Legal, HR, IT, and Finance, to support investigations and implement corrective actions.

  • Stay updated with industry best practices, regulatory changes, and emerging threats in fraud and financial crime.

Required qualifications

  • Minimum 15 years of experience in performing corporate investigations, anti-fraud assessments or similar roles.

  • Expert knowledge of investigative methodologies, forensic accounting principles, fraud detection techniques.

  • Experience of leading overseas Ethics & Compliance or fraud-related fieldwork assignments (proactive or reactive), from planning to reporting, including management of team members, key stakeholders and the management of the target entity.

  • Ability to demonstrate a track record of report writing, presenting to senior management / C-suite level.

  • Experience of leading investigations across a range of fields – Financial, Operational, HR, HSE, Compliance & Ethics.

  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills.

  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple investigations simultaneously. Demonstration of ability to project manage multiple projects in a high-pressure environment. Demonstrably ability to work collaboratively.

  • Proficiency in using forensic tools and software for data analysis.

  • High ethical standards and a commitment to integrity and confidentiality.

  • Understanding of the mining, shipping, and commodity trading industries.

  • Familiarity with financial regulations and compliance standards.

  • Advanced experience and knowledge of current digital forensics and investigation techniques.

  • Excellent English; native or equivalent to C2 level oral and written skills.

Preferred qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Criminal Justice, or a related field. Advanced degree or certifications (e.g., CFE, CPA, CIA) preferred.

Attributes for sucess

  • Personal gravitas to operate comfortably and confidently with Senior Management of the business. Ability to build a network of key contacts within the business, across different offices. Firm, decisive and results oriented.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex information clearly and concisely.

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, demanding work environment, with strong work ethic and ability to meet deadlines.

  • Ability and willingness to travel to meet project demands (anticipated travel expectation is less than 10%).

  • Conversant in multiple languages relevant to Trafigura business considered a plus (Spanish, French, Portuguese, Chinese).

Department overview

As part of a wider investment and strengthening in the areas of Governance, Risk and Controls, Internal Audit and Compliance, in January 2025 the Chief Risk Officer and Global Head of Compliance established a new internal Investigations Team.

The Investigations team, currently a team of four based across Geneva and Athens, works alongside existing functions that support the Governance framework, with a remit to: lead the more sensitive and significant internal investigations; to support Legal in their response to regulatory enquiries; to coordinate and supervise investigations performed by the HR, Compliance or HSE teams; and, to oversee the Trafigura Speak Up channel.

The team is a fact-finding function focused on alleged misconduct by internal or external parties that impact Trafigura’s operations, assets, people or systems. The reactive work undertaken by the team is case-driven, event-specific, independent and confidential, and will often be defensive in nature, to minimise legal or reputational risk.

In addition to its ‘reactive’ work, and in coordination with the Operational Risk team, the Investigations team is tasked with performing forensic reviews of higher-risk markets and activities.

The team reports to the General Counsel and has a dotted line into the CEO and Audit Committee Chair. The team works closely with Trafigura’s Compliance, Internal Audit, Operational Risk and Internal Controls, Security, HR and CHESS teams as part of the wider network of functions charged with protecting the financial and reputational integrity of the company.

Equal opportunity employer

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and take pride in a diverse workforce! We do not discriminate in recruitment, hiring, training, promotion or other employment practices for reasons of race, colour, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, age, marital or veteran status, medical condition or handicap, disability, or any other legally protected status.

title: Data Engineer - COL
description:
Note: To be eligible for this role, you must be based in Medellín, Colombia and able to work from our office three days per week. Working hours are 10:00 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. (Colombia time), Monday to Friday a schedule designed to provide overlap with our teams across multiple U.S. time zones.

About Deckard Technologies

Deckard Technologies is a GovTech data company helping local governments address residential property-related challenges, with a focus on compliance and tax collection. Founded in 2018, we operate globally with offices in the U.S., Colombia, and Australia.

Trusted by over 400 jurisdictions worldwide, our scalable, cost-effective products leverage patented processes and combine best-in-class data collection with intuitive, AI-powered solutions, transforming how local governments monitor and manage properties.

Joining us means you'll be working with a diverse group of inspiring people from industry experts and extraordinary technology and data operations teams to innovative product leaders in a down-to-earth and supportive culture.

Role Overview

We are seeking a Data Engineer to join our operational office in Medellín, Colombia. In this role, you will be responsible for monitoring database health, overseeing end-to-end data pipeline flows, and developing scalable analytics tools, dashboards, and operational workflows within Snowflake and Sigma Computing.

You will work closely with cross-functional Implementation, Data, and Client Experience teams to ensure data integrity, streamline business intelligence delivery, and build self-service reporting assets that drive customer value.

Key Responsibilities

  • Database Monitoring & Data Flow Quality/Oversight: Proactively monitor SQL and cloud data warehouse pipelines, staging tables, and automated data ingestion to ensure continuous availability, high performance, and data integrity.
  • Sigma BI Development: Design, build, and maintain interactive dashboards, complex data workbooks, and custom internal and external reporting tools within Sigma.
  • Data Transformation & Modelling: Write efficient, robust SQL queries, data models, and transformation scripts to prepare raw, multi-source datasets for BI consumption.
  • Troubleshooting & Anomaly Detection: Quickly identify, isolate, and resolve pipeline bottlenecks, data synchronisation failures, broken schemas, or report calculation discrepancies.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Implementation Coordinators, Program Managers, and Data Engineers to structure client-specific data workstreams, including legacy records and spatial data assets.
  • Documentation & Standards: Document data dictionary definitions, metric logic, workflow automations, and reporting best practices to support team scalability.

Required Skills, Qualifications & Experience

  • Snowflake and Sigma Computing: Demonstrated practical experience working with cloud data warehouses and building dashboards and calculation models in Sigma Computing or deep expertise in platforms such as Tableau, Power BI, or Looker, with a strong ability to quickly master Sigma. Experience with cloud data warehouse platforms such as Snowflake, BigQuery, PostgreSQL, or Amazon Redshift is valued, with direct Snowflake experience being highly regarded.
  • Experience: 2–4 years of hands-on experience in data engineering, data analysis, BI development, or database monitoring in a production environment.
  • Advanced SQL—Essential: Strong, hands-on SQL capability is essential for this role. Candidates must be proficient in writing and optimising complex queries using CTEs, window functions, joins, and aggregations across cloud data warehouses such as Snowflake, BigQuery, PostgreSQL, or Amazon Redshift.
  • Data Flow & Pipeline Knowledge: Solid understanding of ETL/ELT principles, database schema design, and tracking data lineage from ingestion through to dashboard display.
  • English and Spanish Language Proficiency: A minimum B2 level of English proficiency, both verbal and written, is required, alongside native or fluent Spanish. This role involves regular communication and collaboration with English-speaking colleagues across the United States and Australia.
  • Problem-Solving: Strong analytical mindset with rigorous attention to detail regarding data accuracy and quality assurance.
  • Analytical & Model Literacy: Comfort working with the outputs of predictive and classification models, such as booked-versus-blocked night inference and occupancy estimates. This includes understanding confidence thresholds, precision and recall trade-offs, known failure modes, and representing predicted values as distinct from observed values in dashboards and client-facing reporting.
  • Data Governance & Confidentiality: Sound judgment when handling sensitive client data and public records containing personally identifiable information, including address-level and parcel-level data. Familiarity with access controls, row-level security, and the principle of exposing only the minimum data a given report or user requires.
  • Communication & Data Storytelling: Ability to explain data limitations, methodology, and confidence levels to non-technical partners, Implementation Coordinators, Program Managers, and client stakeholders in clear terms. You'll be the person who explains what a number does and does not support and translates a schema change or data gap into what it means for a client's deliverable.
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field such as Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, Engineering, or Information Systems—or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • DBT Experience: Experience working with DBT would be an asset, demonstrating exposure to large-scale, modern SQL pipelines and structured data transformation practices.
  • Familiarity with scripting languages for data automation, such as Python, R, or Bash.
  • Experience with GIS or spatial data layers, such as Esri ArcGIS integrations.
  • Prior experience in a SaaS, civic technology, GovTech, or data-intensive analytics start-up environment.
  • Experience working directly with U.S.-based distributed teams.

English-Language Requirement

As this role works closely with colleagues across the United States and Australia, candidates must have a minimum B2 level of English proficiency and be comfortable participating in meetings, discussing technical matters, and communicating clearly in writing.

Equal Opportunity

At Deckard Technologies, we select candidates solely on merit, experience, and suitability for the role, in line with Article 13 of the Political Constitution of Colombia and Law 931 of 2004. The English-language requirement for this position is directly related to the operational responsibilities of the role and the need to collaborate with English-speaking colleagues across the United States and Australia.

We do not discriminate based on age, sex, race, national or family origin, language background, religion, or political or philosophical opinion.

We welcome applications from persons with disabilities and will make reasonable adjustments to our selection process upon request, in keeping with Law 361 of 1997. Deckard is committed to providing a workplace free from harassment and workplace violence, in line with Law 1010 of 2006 and supported by our Comité de Convivencia Laboral.

title: Information Referral Counselor @Virtual Care Center - Nights - Full Time
description:

Position Details:

Behavioral Health Information & Referral Counselor (Nights)

Location: Mercy Virtual Care Center, Chesterfield, MO
Schedule: Full-Time Nights

Position Summary

The Behavioral Health Information & Referral Counselor serves as a critical first point of contact for individuals and families seeking behavioral health services. This role provides assessment, support, education, and referral coordination for callers experiencing mental health and behavioral health concerns. Through compassionate communication and clinical judgment, the counselor connects individuals with the most appropriate treatment resources while ensuring timely care coordination and follow-up.

The ideal candidate is an excellent communicator, skilled problem-solver, and compassionate advocate who can effectively assist individuals in crisis while navigating complex behavioral health systems and community resources.

Key Responsibilities

Patient & Family Support

  • Provide support, education, and guidance to patients, families, and community members seeking behavioral health services.
  • Assess callers' presenting concerns and identify appropriate treatment options and resources.
  • Educate individuals and families on recommended services, treatment programs, and next steps for care.
  • Follow up with high-risk callers and families to encourage connection with recommended services and resources.

Referral & Care Coordination

  • Coordinate assessments and admissions by communicating clinical and financial information to care teams, providers, and admitting physicians.
  • Connect callers with appropriate internal programs and community-based resources.
  • Facilitate transfers and ensure smooth care transitions when a higher level of care is needed.
  • Maintain strong relationships with community agencies and referral partners to support access to care.

Documentation & Communication

  • Accurately document patient information, presenting concerns, referral recommendations, insurance information, and referral sources.
  • Enter and maintain information within departmental databases and systems in a timely manner.
  • Ensure clear communication and handoff information for on-call staff and team members to support continuity of care.
  • Maintain confidentiality and compliance with all privacy regulations and organizational policies.

Quality & Professional Practice

  • Maintain current and accurate referral resource information, including program details, contact information, and insurance participation.
  • Manage calls efficiently while ensuring callers receive thorough support and guidance.
  • Adhere to all safety, infection prevention, patient rights, and regulatory requirements.
  • Participate in departmental initiatives and perform additional duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Counseling, or a related field.

Required Skills & Experience

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to assess, understand, and respond to behavioral health concerns with professionalism and empathy.
  • Excellent telephone assessment and customer service skills.
  • Knowledge of behavioral health services, levels of care, community resources, and insurance processes.
  • Ability to explain complex clinical and service information clearly to callers and families.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize multiple tasks and situations.
  • Ability to work independently and make sound decisions in both routine and complex situations.
  • Proficiency with computer systems, databases, and documentation platforms.

Why Join Us?

As a Behavioral Health Information & Referral Counselor, you'll play an essential role in helping individuals and families access the behavioral health care they need. You'll be part of a collaborative team dedicated to improving lives through compassionate support, timely intervention, and meaningful connections to treatment and community resources.

Why Mercy?

From day one, Mercy offers outstanding benefits - including medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, tuition support, and matched retirement plans for team members working 32+ hours per pay period.

Join a caring, collaborative team where your voice matters. At Mercy, you'll help shape the future of healthcare through innovation, technology, and compassion. As we grow, you'll grow with us.

title: Activity Leader - Early Childhood Program
description:
Why work at Greenwich House?

At Greenwich House, we believe in empowering communities through transformative programs, we offer more than a job – we offer a mission. When you work with us, you become part of a passionate, collaborative team committed to making a difference in people’s lives. Every initiative, class, and outreach effort we deliver is fueled by a shared commitment to equity and compassion.

Founded in 1902 as a settlement house aimed at supporting New York City's growing immigrant population, Greenwich House has since evolved into a dynamic nonprofit organization dedicated to fostering wellness, creativity, and connection across the city. Today, Greenwich House offers a diverse range of programs in health, human services, education, and the arts, serving thousands of New Yorkers each year. Learn more at .

The Opportunity

Youth Services Activity Leaders are responsible for leading high-quality, developmentally appropriate afterschool programming for early childhood-aged children. They design and implement engaging activities that support early learning through creative play, arts, movement, and exploration, while fostering a safe, nurturing, and joyful environment. Activity Leaders serve as the primary classroom lead during afterschool hours and work closely with program staff to ensure smooth daily operations, positive behavior support, and meaningful learning experiences for all children.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is passionate about people and wants to be part of a mission-driven organization making a lasting impact in New York City.

  • Foster a warm, inclusive atmosphere of fun and learning and serve as a positive role model
  • Communicate effectively with program leadership regarding classroom needs, student progress, and daily operations
  • Ensure a safe, clean, and welcoming learning environment at all times
  • Promote positive character development, cooperation, and respectful behavior among all children

What You’ll Bring

  • Must be responsible, reliable and punctual

  • A genuine enthusiasm for working with early childhood aged children and supporting their social, emotional, and developmental growth

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
description:
Job Title

Postdoctoral Research Associate

Agency

Texas A&M Agrilife Research

Department

Rangeland, Wildlife & Fisheries Management

Proposed Minimum Salary

Commensurate

Job Location

College Station, Texas

Job Type

Job Description

About Texas A&M AgriLife

Texas A&M AgriLife is comprised of the following Texas A&M University System members:

  • Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service

  • Texas A&M AgriLife Research

  • College of Agriculture and Life Sciences at Texas A&M University

  • Texas A&M Forest Service

  • Texas A&M Veterinary Medical Diagnostic Laboratory

As the nation’s largest most comprehensive agriculture program, Texas A&M AgriLife brings together a college and four state agencies focused on agriculture and life sciences within The Texas A&M University System. With over 5,000 employees and a presence in every county across the state, Texas A&M AgriLife is uniquely positioned to improve lives, environments and the Texas economy through education, research, extension and service.

Click here to learn more about how you can be a part of AgriLife and make a difference in the world!

Position Information

The Texas A&M Center for Grazinglands and Ranch Management (CGRM) is seeking a Post-Doctoral Researcher to support applied research projects focused on grazing management and soil health. This position will lead the analysis and interpretation of soil data already collected across multiple projects spanning working rangelands in Texas, Oklahoma, Hawaii, and Arizona. These datasets represent a range of ecological contexts and management systems and provide an opportunity to evaluate soil health responses across various grazingland environments.

The successful candidate will work with soil physical, chemical, and biological datasets derived from both laboratory analyses and near-infrared spectroscopy. In addition to leading data analysis, this individual will contribute to interpretation, manuscript development, publication, and communication of findings to scientific and producer audiences.

Texas A&M University’s Center for Grazinglands and Ranch Management aims to strengthen the ecological and economic resiliency of grazinglands and ranching operations through producer-directed, applied research, outreach, and industry engagement. CGRM develops interdisciplinary collaborations to address critical needs in the ranching community and works to enhance operational resiliency, strengthen enterprise sustainability, and support the future of the grazinglands industry.

The Postdoctoral Research Associate is responsible for conducting and communicating research on soil health and grazing management, including data analysis, evaluation of soil health indicators, and dissemination of findings through publications, presentations, and stakeholder engagement.

Responsibilities:

  • Analyze and interpret soil physical, chemical, and biological data.

  • Evaluate the effectiveness of near-infrared spectroscopy for estimating key soil health characteristics.

  • Assess the influence of grazing management on soil health indicators.

  • Prepare peer-reviewed manuscripts and conference presentations based on project findings.

  • Communicate research findings to stakeholders, and livestock producer audiences.

  • Contribute to the development of future research questions, analyses, and project outputs related to grazing management and soil health.

  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • PhD in rangeland management, soil science, natural resource management, environmental science, ecology, or a related field

  • Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research, as evidenced by peer-reviewed publications

  • Experience analyzing and interpreting complex environmental, agricultural, or ecological datasets

  • Ability and willingness to engage with applied research questions and interact professionally with livestock producers and other stakeholders

  • Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate research findings to both scientific and producer audiences

  • Demonstrated ability to work independently, take initiative, and manage projects with limited supervision

  • Strong quantitative, analytical, and problem-solving skills

  • Ability to organize, manage, and interpret complex datasets with attention to detail

  • Ability to connect research findings to real-world management questions and working lands decision-making

  • Ability to lead data analysis, manuscript preparation, and dissemination of research findings

Other Requirements:

  • This position is funded through grants or contracts. Continued employment is dependent upon ongoing funding and satisfactory job performance.

What You Need to Know

Salary: Compensation is commensurate with the candidate’s qualifications.

Position Funding: This position is funded through grants or contracts. Continued employment is dependent upon ongoing funding and satisfactory job performance.

Why Work at Texas A&M AgriLife?

When you choose to work for Texas A&M AgriLife, you become part of an organization that is an established leader in agriculture and life sciences with a wide range of capabilities to meet the needs of our statewide, national, and international constituents.

In addition, Texas A&M AgriLife offers a comprehensive benefit package including the following:

title: Software/Data Engineer
description:
We are seeking a hands-on Software cum Data Engineer to design, develop, and maintain backend applications, APIs, data integration services, and data pipelines. The role requires strong software engineering capabilities, particularly in Node.js and RESTful API development, combined with practical experience in databases and data engineering.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain RESTful APIs and backend services using Node.js.
  • Develop reusable microservices and integration components to support application and data requirements.
  • Build and maintain data pipelines (ETL/ELT) for ingestion, transformation, processing, and movement of structured and unstructured data.
  • Integrate applications with databases, external systems, APIs, and enterprise platforms.
  • Design API specifications, data models, schemas, and interface contracts.
  • Implement API authentication and authorization, including OAuth 2.0, JWT, and role-based access controls.
  • Develop solutions using relational and NoSQL databases such as PostgreSQL, or Elasticsearch.

  • Implement logging, monitoring, exception handling, audit trails, and performance optimisation.
  • Develop automated unit, integration, and API tests.
  • Work closely with solution architects, data engineers, software developers, DevOps engineers, and business analysts.

Technical Requirements

Essential

  • Degree/Diploma in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Data Engineering, or related discipline.
  • Strong hands-on development experience with Node.js and JavaScript.
  • Strong experience designing and developing REST APIs.
  • Good knowledge of SQL and database design.
  • Experience integrating multiple systems and data sources.
  • Understanding of JSON, HTTP/HTTPS, OpenAPI/Swagger, OAuth 2.0 and JWT.
  • Experience with Git and CI/CD practices.
  • Good understanding of software engineering principles, design patterns, and secure coding.

Good to Have

  • Python for data engineering and automation.
  • Event/message streaming technologies.
  • Elasticsearch
  • API gateways
  • Docker and Kubernetes.

Preferred Experience

  • 3-6 years of relevant software development/data engineering experience, with demonstrated ability to independently develop backend services and APIs and work across both application and data layers.

Our client, a large Perth based organisation running a significant enterprise wide AI programme, is looking for a Practice Lead, AI / Automation to identify, build and scale practical AI and automation solutions across the business, and drive measurable productivity outcomes from their AI tools.

This is a technical, hands on role suited to someone who has come up through a technical career, engineering, data, software or platform background, and has moved into AI adoption and automation leadership as that shift has become the more valuable place to apply their skills. You'll need genuine fluency in how LLMs and automation tools actually work under the hood, so you can assess workflows, design solutions, configure and integrate tools, and prove out real productivity gains, not just run workshops.

What you'll do
  • Assess business workflows across teams and identify where LLM based tools, automation or RPA can realistically remove manual effort and improve output quality
  • Design, configure and implement AI and automation solutions using enterprise platforms (LLM based chat tools, Copilot style tools, workflow automation and RPA platforms)
  • Apply solid understanding of LLM architecture, prompt engineering, context management, RAG and model limitations to build reliable, repeatable solutions and prompt patterns
  • Build technical playbooks and reusable prompt/automation templates that teams can apply directly to their own use cases
  • Define and track technical usage and productivity metrics (prompt quality, task completion, tool utilisation, session data) using platform analytics and reporting tools
  • Partner with professional functions (e.g. legal, finance) to map current processes, scope automation opportunities and deliver working solutions
  • Provide technical troubleshooting on tool configuration, prompt performance and integration issues, escalating platform level problems where required
  • Report on adoption, usage and productivity outcomes against an executive mandated target, backed by data
What you bring
  • A technical background (software engineering, data engineering, platform, systems or similar) with several years hands on delivery experience before moving into AI/automation focused work
  • Genuine hands on experience building or deploying AI/automation solutions, not a pure trainer, facilitator or change management background
  • Strong working knowledge of generative AI and LLM concepts (prompting, context windows, model limitations, RAG, fine tuning at a conceptual level) with the ability to apply them practically
  • Hands on experience with enterprise AI platforms (e.g. Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise, Grok or similar) and/or workflow automation tools (e.g. Power Automate, RPA platforms, scripting/no code tooling)
  • Experience scoping and delivering automation or AI use cases end to end, from workflow assessment through to working solution
  • Comfortable working close to the technical detail (basic scripting, API level understanding, or low code/no code platform configuration) while still communicating clearly with non technical stakeholders
  • Self directed, low supervision operator who can build and scale a technical programs.

SUMMARY:

The Program Director of Educator Preparation Clinical Initiatives, under general supervision, coordinates and supports clinical experience initiatives within educator preparation programs. The position serves as the primary liaison among school district partners, the Office of Educator Certification, the Department of Curriculum and Instruction, and other stakeholders to facilitate clinical placements, support mentor teacher and supervisor development, monitor candidate progress, and collect data to support continuous program improvement. This position will be primarily located at the Dallas location with occasional travel to the main campus.

This position is grant funded through 08/31/2029. Continued employment is contingent upon funding renewal.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Oversee the coordination of clinical placements for teacher candidates with school districts and educational partners across the state.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for school district personnel regarding clinical experiences, placements, and partnership activities.
  • Coordinate and oversee training and support for mentor teachers and university field supervisors to ensure effective supervision of teacher candidates.
  • Serve as a liaison between the Office of Educator Certification and school districts to facilitate the completion and submission of required certification and clinical experience documentation.
  • Serve as a liaison between the Department of Curriculum and Instruction and program advisors to communicate Texas Education Agency (TEA) requirements, policy changes, and educator preparation program updates.
  • Coordinate with College of Innovation and Design Student Success Team on student matters including, but not limited to, academic advising and clinical teaching application completion.
  • Monitor teacher candidate growth and progress throughout clinical experiences and assist in identifying and addressing areas of concern.
  • Provide guidance, training, and support to university field supervisors regarding clinical experience expectations, assessment processes, and candidate development.
  • Coordinate planning and participate in advisory meetings with school district and community partners to strengthen educator preparation partnerships and support continuous program improvement.
  • Collect, maintain, analyze, and report data related to clinical placements, candidate performance, and partnership effectiveness.
  • Assist with educator preparation and Academic Affairs initiatives as assigned.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

  • Education: Master's degree in Education, Educational Leadership, Curriculum and Instruction, Higher Education Administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Experience: Three years of experience in educator preparation, K-12 education, field-based teacher education, clinical supervision, program administration, or a related area.
  • Knowledge / Skills / Abilities:
  • Knowledge of educator preparation programs, clinical teaching requirements, and state certification regulations.
  • Knowledge of Texas Education Agency policies and educator certification processes.
  • Knowledge of data collection, reporting, and continuous improvement practices.
  • Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Ability to develop and maintain collaborative relationships with school district personnel, faculty, staff, mentor teachers, and community partners.
  • Ability to organize multiple projects, manage complex processes, and meet deadlines.
  • Ability to analyze data and prepare reports to support program assessment and improvement efforts.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
  • Proficiency with word processing, spreadsheet, database, and student information systems.
  • Licensing/Professional Certifications: Valid Texas Teaching Certificate; Valid driver’s license
  • Physical Requirements: None
  • Other Requirements: Possible travel to partner school disticts

PREFERRED EDUCATION / SKILLS/ EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience working with educator preparation programs and clinical teaching placements.
  • Experience collaborating with PK-12 school districts and educational partners.
  • Experience providing training, coaching, or supervision to educators.
  • Familiarity with accreditation, assessment, and continuous improvement processes related to educator preparation programs.

SUPERVISION OF OTHERS:

Supervision of university field supervisors.

WHY WORK AT EAST TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY?

Competitive Benefits & Work-Life Balance:

  • Employee tuition assistance for master’s and doctoral programs.
  • Comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, vision, life, and long-term disability insurance.
  • ETAMU contributes to employee health and basic life insurance premiums.
  • 12-15 days of annual paid holidays, plus up to eight hours of paid sick leave and vacation each month.
  • Automatic enrollment in the Teacher Retirement System of Texas (TRS), with optional additional retirement plans (ORP).
  • Physical wellness program and wellness release time for eligible employees.

Career Growth & Development:

  • Access to cutting-edge research opportunities at a designated R2 Research Institution.

Academic Excellence:

  • ETAMU is ranked among the top 30% in five online degree programs and offers national recognized academic programs.
  • Over 140 degree programs, including nationally ranked online and graduate options.

Agency

Commensurate

Job Description

About Texas A&M AgriLife

Texas A&M AgriLife is comprised of the following Texas A&M University System members:

  • Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service

  • Texas A&M AgriLife Research

  • College of Agriculture and Life Sciences at Texas A&M University

  • Texas A&M Forest Service

  • Texas A&M Veterinary Medical Diagnostic Laboratory

As the nation’s largest most comprehensive agriculture program, Texas A&M AgriLife brings together a college and four state agencies focused on agriculture and life sciences within The Texas A&M University System. With over 5,000 employees and a presence in every county across the state, Texas A&M AgriLife is uniquely positioned to improve lives, environments and the Texas economy through education, research, extension and service.

Click here to learn more about how you can be a part of AgriLife and make a difference in the world!

Position Information

The Texas A&M Center for Grazinglands and Ranch Management is seeking a Research Associate with a strong work ethic to assist in executing projects related to exclusion fencing and mitigation of wild pig damage.

Texas A&M University’s Center for Grazinglands and Ranch Management (CGRM) aims to safeguard the ecologic and economic resiliency of grazingland resources and ranching operations with a focus on producer-directed, applied grazingland and ranch management research, outreach, and industry engagement. CGRM develops and supports interdisciplinary collaborations to address critical needs in the ranching community and strives to achieve three overarching goals: enhance operational resiliency, strengthen enterprise sustainability, and foster the future of the industry.

The Senior Research Associate is responsible for conducting field-based wildlife research and wild pig management activities across Texas, including data collection, monitoring, stakeholder coordination, and project support. This position works closely with landowners and project partners to implement and evaluate research and damage mitigation efforts.

Responsibilities:

  • Responsible for working directly with landowners, managers, biologists, ranchers, and a wide range of constituents.

  • Responsible for all field related work such as identifying study sites, collecting baseline data, setting, filling and maintaining corn feeders, building small exclusion fences and plots, monitoring animal activity with remotely triggered cameras, reviewing and assimilating data from pictures and video, data entry, and report writing.

  • May work with other project collaborators to design and implement wild pig exclusion methods in livestock operations to prevent damage, use of feed and water, and access to sensitive areas, which also may include use of farm equipment, implements, ATVs, UTVs, and similar to remediate damage from wild pigs.

  • Frequent communication with landowners and coordination with project partners, so effective communication skills are required.

  • Travel to multiple study locations across Texas.

  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in relevant field

  • Four years of related professional experience

  • Strong work ethic and self-motivated

  • Ability to work in a remote location, sometimes under adverse conditions (hot, humid, biting/stinging insects), on working ranches with livestock operations

  • Ability to work independently and as a team with minimum supervision and be capable of planning an effective work day

  • Ability to analyze data and write reports

  • Ability to communicate effectively and efficiently (verbal and written);

  • Detail oriented

  • Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others

  • Ability to learn new skills and techniques

Preferred Qualifications:

  • M.S. degree in rangeland management, natural resource management or closely related field; GPA of ≥3.0; more than two years of experience

  • Experience or working knowledge of ranching, wildlife, and rangeland management practices

  • Experience working directly with producers

  • Experience building various fence designs

  • Experience using 4-wheel drive vehicles, ATVs/UTVs, farm machinery/tractors, and ability to tow trailers

  • Knowledge or experience planning, coordinating, and conducting field activities

  • Technical writing skills

Other Requirements:

  • This position is funded through grants or contracts. Continued employment is dependent upon ongoing funding and satisfactory job performance.

What You Need to Know

Salary: Compensation is commensurate with the candidate’s qualifications.

Position Funding: This position is funded through grants or contracts. Continued employment is dependent upon ongoing funding and satisfactory job performance.

Why Work at Texas A&M AgriLife?

When you choose to work for Texas A&M AgriLife, you become part of an organization that is an established leader in agriculture and life sciences with a wide range of capabilities to meet the needs of our statewide, national, and international constituents.

title: Information Security Officer
description:
The Information Security Officer (ISO) owns and is accountable for the credit union’s written Information Security Program (ISP), ensuring compliance with NCUA regulations (12 CFR Part 748), the GLBA Safeguards Rule, and applicable federal and state cybersecurity requirements. The ISO works in partnership with the credit union’s outsourced CISO partner (OneStep), the Information Security Governance Committee, and IT Security to direct the program’s execution, while retaining ultimate accountability to the Board, the VP of Enterprise Risk Management, and NCUA examiners. The ISO also partners with the VP of ERM to lead the credit union’s transition toward an internal information security department. The ISO provides independent oversight and challenge of information security and establishes information security governance and risk requirements.


Key Responsibilities

  • Own and maintain the written Information Security Program (ISP), incorporating guidance from OneStep and the Information Security Governance Committee, with accountability for the program’s adequacy to the Board, VP of ERM, and NCUA examiners.
  • Conduct annual risk assessments of information systems, third-party vendors, and data flows.
  • Oversee the incident response plan (IRP), including compliance with the NCUA 72-hour cyber incident notification rule.
  • Direct vulnerability management, penetration testing, and patch management programs, coordinating execution across external IS consultants and IT Security.
  • Lead vendor/third-party risk management for cloud, core processor, and fintech relationships, including ongoing due diligence and performance monitoring of OneStep as a critical vendor.
  • Align business continuity/disaster recovery planning with information security controls.
  • Deliver information security awareness training and phishing simulation programs to staff and the Board.
  • Serve as primary point of contact for NCUA/state examiners on IT and cybersecurity exams, including the ACET (Automated Cybersecurity Examination Tool) process.
  • Serve as the credit union’s primary internal liaison to the outsourced CISO (external consultant), translating security guidance and recommendations into internal policy, procedures, and Board reporting.
  • Serve as an active member of the Information Security Governance Committee, coordinating between external consultant’s CISO recommendations and internal execution via IT Security.
  • Partner with the VP of Enterprise Risk Management to lead the transition from outsourced information security support (external consultant) to an internal information security department, including org design, staffing plan, and phased capability build-out.
  • Collaborate with the VP of ERM on decisions regarding which functions remain outsourced to external consultant versus insourced as the department matures.
  • Integrate information security risk into the enterprise risk register and ERM reporting cycle, in coordination with the VP of Enterprise Risk Management.
  • Ensure escalation to the Board/Risk Committee is preserved: ISP updates and material risk findings are escalated through the VP of ERM for inclusion in Board/Risk Committee reporting at least annually, with direct Board access maintained for significant incidents or unresolved risk disagreements.
  • Establish Information Security requirements for cloud, SaaS hosted, and externally managed environments, including identity, encryption, logging, configuration management, data protection, and third-party connectivity.
  • Monitor cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities, regulatory alerts, financial-sector threat intelligence, and emerging technology risks, and assess their relevance and potential impact to the credit union.


Job Skills

  • ISO Standards
  • Presentations
  • Access Management Governance
  • Incident Response and Cyber Resilience
  • Regulatory Examination and Audit Management
  • Executive and Board Reporting
  • Control Objectives for Information and Related Technologies (COBIT)
  • Security Technologies and Architecture
  • Risk Management Frameworks
  • Attention to Detail
  • Continuous Learning
  • Facilitation
  • Vendor Management
  • Identity Management Governance
  • Cloud and SaaS Security


Qualifications & Experience

  • 7+ years of progressively responsible experience in information security, cybersecurity, technology risk, information security governance, or a related discipline, with financial-services experience strongly preferred and credit-union experience highly desirable.
  • Working knowledge of NCUA Part 748, GLBA, FFIEC guidance, and the ACET, NIST or equivalent framework.
  • Three plus years in a leadership or supervisory capacity within information security, IT risk, or a related discipline required (e.g., team lead, security manager, or comparable supervisory role) recommended.
  • Experience building or scaling an internal information security function, including staffing and organizational design, strongly preferred.
  • Experience working within an enterprise risk management framework preferred.
  • CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional), CISM (Certified Information Security Manager) or equivalent senior information security certification required, CISSP and CISM combination preferred.
  • CRISC (Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control) preferred.
  • CISA (Certified Information Systems Auditor) preferred.
  • GIAC (Global Information Assurance) / GSEC (GIAC Security Essentials) certifications preferred.
  • CCSK (Certificate of Cloud Security Knowledge) /CCSP (Certified Cloud Security Professional) preferred.
  • CGRC (Certified in Governance, Risk and Compliance) preferred.
  • Computer Science (Bachelor's degree) or Information Security (Bachelor's degree) or Information Technology (Bachelor's degree) or equivalent experience.


Minimum Physical Requirements and Working Conditions

  • Sitting for prolonged periods at a desk working on a computer.
  • Frequent prolonged meetings in person or online.
  • Traveling to various branches on occasion.
  • Reaching, bending, twisting, turning on occasion.
  • Lifting, pulling, pushing, and carrying up to 30 pounds on occasion.
  • We'll make reasonable accommodations for qualified applicants and employees with disabilities.


Benefits and Pay

The expected pay for the Information Security Officer (ISO) is $110,667.18 to $150,000.24 per year.


This pay reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer for this role based on typical qualifications and market data. Offered pay may vary depending on the candidate’s experience, skills, and other relevant factors.


We cover 100% of employees single medical, drug, vision, and dental monthly health insurance premiums. Employees also love receiving paid volunteer time and our pay it forward program. Tuition assistance for higher education is another special way we invest in our workforce. Benefits include, Paid Time Off, 401(k) and 3% Employer Contribution, Health insurance, Paid time off, Vision insurance, Dental insurance, Prescription drug insurance, Tuition reimbursement, Life insurance, Flexible spending account, Disability insurance, Health savings account, Opportunities for advancement, Employee assistance program, Referral program, Retirement plan, Employee discount, Paid training, Professional development assistance, AD&D insurance, Volunteer time off, Credit union membership, Paid orientation, and more.


Make a difference one life at a time!

title: Lead Developer with deep AWS, Node.js, TypeScript and Ai expertise to lead the design and delivery of highly scalable API services supporting enterprise lending and data platforms.
description:
Lead Developer with deep AWS, Node.js, TypeScript and Ai expertise to lead the design and delivery of highly scalable API services supporting enterprise lending and data platforms.

Lead Developer with deep AWS, Node.js, TypeScript and Ai expertise to lead the design and delivery of highly scalable API services supporting enterprise lending and data platforms.

Duration: 6 Months

Location: Toronto, Hybrid (2x/week)

Overview:

We are seeking a Lead Developer with deep AWS, Node.js and TypeScript expertise to lead the design and delivery of highly scalable API services supporting enterprise lending and data platforms within a large financial institution.

The ideal candidate will be a hands-on technical lead with strong cloud-native engineering fundamentals who is also at the forefront of AI-enabled software development. This includes demonstrated experience establishing AI development harnesses, leveraging coding agents and agentic workflows, and implementing rigorous validation frameworks to ensure AI-generated code is reliable, secure and production-ready.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the architecture, design and hands-on development of scalable, highly available API services using Node.js, TypeScript and AWS.
  • Design and implement cloud-native solutions leveraging AWS Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB and related AWS services.
  • Provide technical leadership across solution design, development, testing, deployment and production support.
  • Evaluate architectural and engineering trade-offs and make sound technical decisions balancing scalability, maintainability, delivery timelines and complexity.
  • Build solutions with a high degree of automation that are supportable, reusable and aligned with enterprise engineering standards.
  • Establish and evolve AI-assisted software engineering workflows, including development harnesses, coding agents and automated feedback loops.
  • Define approaches for validating AI-generated code before it is accepted into the codebase, including deterministic validation through automated testing, type checking, static analysis, linting, security scanning and other programmatic quality gates.
  • Develop agentic workflows that can iteratively generate, test, evaluate and refine software based on objective validation results.
  • Determine appropriate guardrails, context, tooling and engineering standards for the effective use of AI throughout the software development lifecycle.
  • Proactively diagnose and resolve complex production issues and perform root-cause analysis.
  • Collaborate with business, architecture and technology stakeholders to translate requirements into effective technical solutions.
  • Mentor developers, establish engineering best practices and raise the technical capability of the broader team.

Must Haves:

  • Advanced AWS development experience, including:
  • AWS Lambda
  • API Gateway
  • DynamoDB
  • AWS SDK
  • AWS CDK
  • Experience designing and implementing high-volume, highly available and highly automated applications.
  • Strong API and distributed systems design fundamentals.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate as a hands-on technical lead, including architecture/design decisions, development, troubleshooting and mentoring.
  • Strong understanding of software engineering principles, design patterns, automated testing and production-grade development practices.
  • Demonstrated advanced use of AI-assisted software development, beyond basic code completion or prompt usage.
  • Experience establishing or configuring AI development harnesses, including how models or agents receive context, instructions, tools, constraints and feedback.
  • Hands-on experience using or developing coding agents and agentic engineering workflows for activities such as implementation, testing, debugging, refactoring or code review.
  • Experience implementing structured methods to validate AI-generated code and outputs before they are accepted or deployed.
  • Strong understanding of deterministic validation, including the use of automated tests, compilation/type checking, linting, static analysis, security checks, contract validation or other objective quality gates to determine whether generated code is correct.
  • Ability to explain how AI-generated output is evaluated, how failures are fed back into agent workflows, and how engineering quality is maintained when using AI extensively.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills with the ability to make and defend technical trade-offs.

Nice to Haves:

  • Experience with Amazon Bedrock or other enterprise LLM platforms.
  • Experience with MCP, tool-enabled agents or multi-agent development workflows.
  • Experience integrating AI agents with CI/CD or broader SDLC automation.
  • Experience developing reusable prompt, context or agent frameworks for engineering teams.
  • Knowledge of LLM evaluation, observability, guardrails and responsible AI practices.
  • Previous experience within banking, lending, payments or other highly regulated enterprise environments.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or equivalent industry experience.

Disclaimer: AI may be used in evaluating candidates.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

title: Data Engineer - Platform & Analytics
description:
We are looking for a Data Engineer – Platform & Analytics to join our regional edge platform data team supporting digital business across Asia-Pacific. This role sits within a technical team closely aligned with application development and is responsible for delivering end-to-end data solutions, including application databases, data lakehouse platforms, data pipelines, data sharing, and business reporting.

The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting and enhancing our data ecosystem while partnering with business stakeholders, application teams, and regional data consumers to deliver reliable, scalable, and high-quality data solutions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and maintain data pipelines and ETL/ELT processes.
  • Support and optimize cloud-based data platforms, databases, and data lakehouses.
  • Build scalable data integration solutions across multiple source systems.
  • Ensure data quality, reliability, monitoring, and operational excellence across data assets.
  • Manage data ingestion, transformation, and data delivery processes.

Database Administration & Support

  • Support application databases and perform database troubleshooting.
  • Assist with database performance tuning, access management, and operational support.
  • Implement data security, governance, and compliance requirements.
  • Support deployment, release activities, and production issue resolution.

Analytics & Reporting

  • Collaborate with business stakeholders to understand reporting requirements.
  • Develop and support dashboards, reports, and analytical datasets.
  • Translate business requirements into scalable data models and reporting solutions.
  • Enable self-service reporting through well-structured and governed datasets.

Platform Governance & Continuous Improvement

  • Contribute to data standards, best practices, and solution standardization initiatives.
  • Implement monitoring, alerting, and operational controls for data solutions.
  • Support automation and AI-driven opportunities to improve delivery efficiency.
  • Participate in architecture reviews and platform improvement initiatives.

Required Skills & Experience

Technical Skills

  • Strong SQL development and query optimization skills.
  • Experience with relational databases such as PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL server
  • Experience building and maintaining ETL/ELT pipelines.
  • Experience with cloud data platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Databricks.
  • Familiarity with data warehouse concepts and dimensional modelling.
  • Experience with reporting and visualization tools such as Power BI.
  • Exposure to version control tools such as Git.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with Databricks, Delta Lake, and Spark.
  • Experience with AWS services such as Glue, S3, Lambda, and IAM.
  • Knowledge of data governance, security, and access control practices.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD and DevOps practices.
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools such as GitHub Copilot.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Data Engineering, or a related field.
  • 3–7 years of experience in data engineering, database development, or analytics engineering.
  • Experience working in Agile delivery environments is preferred.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver under tight timelines.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.
  • Strong ownership mindset and accountability.
  • Continuous learning attitude with a willingness to explore new technologies and AI capabilities.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across regional teams.

What You'll Gain

  • Exposure to regional APAC data initiatives.
  • Opportunity to work across data engineering, platform operations, and analytics.
  • Hands-on experience with modern cloud and data technologies.
  • Opportunities for career growth through role ownership and specialization.
  • Involvement in strategic data and AI initiatives supporting business transformation.

The Contract New Business Developer is a Contract Sales-aligned new business leadership role responsible for driving profitable growth by identifying, developing, and securing larger, complex contract opportunities across Local Contract Customers (LC1) and select Corporate Multi-Unit (CMU) segments. The role focuses on planned, pipeline-driven growth and partners closely with Region Vice Presidents of Contract Sales, the National Sales New Business Development Team, Region Contract Managers, Region Bid Sales Managers, Market Vice Presidents of Contract Sales, Customer Experience, Specialty and other cross-functional stakeholders to deliver integrated, customer-centric solutions.

Leveraging advanced analytics, disciplined opportunity management, and a team-based selling approach, the Contract New Business Developer builds and manages a credible pipeline of high-value prospects, coordinates proposal and contract development activities, and leads strategic engagements from initial targeting through contract execution. This role requires a strong understanding of contract sales models, compliance requirements, and complex customer needs, with an emphasis on concept-level thinking, multi-location growth strategies, and long-term customer value creation.

The Contract New Business Developer plays a critical role in accelerating Contract Sales growth by ensuring the right opportunities are pursued with focus, rigor, and cross-functional alignment, while transitioning successfully awarded business into sustained execution and ownership within the Contract Sales organization.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Drive profitable new business growth by identifying, targeting, and securing larger, complex contract sales opportunities in alignment with Contract Sales strategy and financial objectives.
  • Build, manage, and maintain a disciplined, credible new business pipeline focused on higher-value contract opportunities by leveraging advanced analytics, market insights, and strategic prospect targeting to prioritize effort and maximize conversion.
  • Lead complex, team-based selling efforts by partnering closely with Region Contract Managers, Region Bid Sales Managers, Contract Sales leadership, Market Contract Sales leadership, Customer Experience, Specialty, and other cross-functional teams to develop integrated, customer-focused solutions that meet prospect needs.
  • Coordinate and manage proposal, bid, and contract development activities for targeted opportunities, ensuring accuracy, value alignment, and compliance with pricing, contracting, and approval requirements while supporting timely execution and decision-making.
  • Engage Regional Vice Presidents of Contract Sales and other contract sales leadership to review pipeline performance, assess opportunity health, identify risks or barriers, and align on actions required to advance strategic opportunities.
  • Lead strategic prospect engagement from initial targeting through contract award, including conducting discovery, presenting value propositions, negotiating terms as appropriate, and supporting a smooth transition of awarded business into ongoing Contract Sales execution and ownership.

Qualifications

Education Required: High School Diploma or GED

Education Preferred: 4-year bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Sales, Marketing, Hospitality or Culinary Arts, Finance, Accounting or related field

Experience Required: 3+ years of relevant sales experience in a business-to-business professional sales environment

Experience Preferred: 3+ years of relevant sales experience in a contract sales role within foodservice distribution, and 2 or more years with a proven track record of new business development

Skills and Abilities:

  • Strong consultative selling and business development skills, with the ability to identify, position, and secure complex contract opportunities with sophisticated customers
  • Demonstrated ability to manage disciplined sales pipelines, leveraging analytics and insights to prioritize opportunities and drive consistent conversion

Data Engineer III

About the Role
We're looking for a Data Engineer III to join our Data Engineering team, which builds and governs the data foundation that powers the business. You'll work within our stack — Python ingestion pipelines, Airflow orchestration, and Snowflake/Databricks — helping move data reliably and securely from source to decision-ready output.
You'll implement features and fixes against a given design, handle known classes of pipeline issues on your own, and escalate genuinely novel problems with clear context rather than working them in isolation. You're also expected to start contributing meaningfully in code review — catching real bugs, not just style nits.

What You'll Do

  • Implement new ingestion sources end-to-end against a senior engineer's design — connector code, DAG, schema, monitoring, and catalog registration — extending the team's existing framework where a new source needs a pattern it doesn't yet support

  • Investigate pipeline failures independently, recognize known classes of issues, and ship the documented fix without needing to escalate

  • Before shipping a new pipeline, identify downstream consumers and what would break if data were late or wrong, and flag gaps like this during spec review — before writing code

  • Write clear handovers when escalating a genuinely unresolved issue — what you tried, what you ruled out, and where things diverge — so a senior can pick up without re-discovery

  • Review peers' pipeline PRs and catch non-obvious issues (e.g., missing idempotency checks, race conditions) that could cause incorrect downstream data

  • Turn ambiguous "why is this data wrong?" questions into structured investigations — tracing data lineage from source to warehouse and communicating back what you found

  • Surface concerns in spec review as specific, well-reasoned questions rather than staying silent or blocking progress

  • Support data security and governance work (e.g., PII masking, access controls) and contribute to data delivery work, including reverse ETL integrations

  • Build strong working relationships with internal stakeholders and help scope and clarify requirements for new work

  • Mentor DE2s on their first significant projects — pairing on tricky decisions and helping them apply team conventions

What We're Looking For

  • 3–5 years of professional software or data engineering experience

  • Strong SQL and Python skills, with solid experience building and operating production data pipelines

  • Comfort investigating and root-causing pipeline issues independently before escalating

  • Experience with workflow orchestration tools (Airflow or similar) and a cloud data warehouse/lakehouse (Snowflake, Databricks, or similar)

  • Solid understanding of data pipeline concepts: idempotency, schema evolution, backfills, and data quality/testing

  • Experience giving substantive code review feedback, not just style or formatting comments

  • Strong communication skills — can write a clear technical handover, ask sharp questions in spec review, and explain a data lineage investigation to a non-technical stakeholder

  • A track record of taking ownership of known-class problems end-to-end rather than needing step-by-step direction


Nice to Have


  • Experience extending or building reusable pipeline frameworks/templates

  • Exposure to reverse ETL tools or patterns, PII masking, or data access governance (RBAC)

  • Exposure to observability/monitoring tooling (e.g., Datadog) for pipeline health and alerting

  • Some experience mentoring or informally supporting more junior engineers

  • Background in gaming, betting, e-commerce, or another regulated/high-compliance industry


Why Join Us


  • Real ownership over known-class problems, with senior/staff support available for the genuinely novel ones

  • Work on high-visibility, high-trust systems that the business depends on

  • A culture built around clear tenets: standardize before you scale, own the outcome (not just the ticket), and clarity over complexity

  • Clear growth path into Senior Data Engineer, with room to start mentoring and shaping team practices along the way
