title: Vice President, Land & Joint Mission Systems
description:
At General Dynamics Mission Systems–International, we do more than engineer technology, we deliver mission-critical capabilities that strengthen national security, enhance allied readiness, and help protect the people we serve.

We are seeking a Vice President, Land & Joint Mission Systems to lead and grow a strategically important global portfolio of integrated land and joint mission capabilities. This is an opportunity to shape the next phase of the business, accelerate innovation and modernization, and deliver solutions that matter to Canada and its allies.

The opportunity

As a key member of the leadership team, you will be accountable for the performance and growth of a complex international business, overseeing strategy, customer engagement, program execution, engineering, and operations.

You will set a clear direction for the portfolio, translate evolving customer, market, technology, and geopolitical developments into decisive business action, and connect capabilities across functions and regions. You will also lead the delivery of complex, multi-year systems integration programs while building trusted relationships with defence customers, government stakeholders, and industry partners in Canada and internationally.

This role calls for a visible, energetic executive who can think strategically, move with pace, and turn complexity into focused execution.

What you will lead

  • Own portfolio performance, including revenue, margin, forecasting, operational outcomes, and sustainable profitability.
  • Develop and execute a growth strategy that strengthens market position, advances major pursuits, and expands into adjacent and international opportunities.
  • Shape investment priorities by rapidly assessing customer needs, market signals, emerging technologies, competitive dynamics, and geopolitical trends.
  • Provide executive oversight of complex global programs from concept through delivery, ensuring strong governance and disciplined management of risk, quality, safety, regulatory, and contractual commitments.
  • Remove barriers, accelerate decisions, and align cross-functional teams around the business’s most critical priorities.
  • Build senior-level relationships with Canadian and international defence customers, government stakeholders, and strategic partners.
  • Advance innovation, modernization, operational excellence, and the adoption of new technologies and delivery approaches.
  • Develop a strong leadership team and foster a culture of accountability, inclusion, collaboration, resilience, and high performance.

You are an accomplished executive with experience leading a significant business, portfolio, or operating unit within defence, aerospace, or another complex, regulated engineering environment. You combine strong commercial judgement with systems thinking, customer insight, and a record of delivering results.

You will bring:

  • Accountability for substantial organizational and financial performance.
  • Experience leading complex systems integration programs across the full lifecycle.
  • A track record of balancing profitable growth, operational performance, and program execution.
  • Strong knowledge of defence acquisition, capability development, and government stakeholder environments.
  • Experience navigating multinational organizations, international partnerships, and cross-border contracts.
  • The ability to synthesize complex information quickly and make sound decisions in ambiguous, fast-moving situations.
  • A record of building capable leadership teams, developing talent, and creating high-performance cultures.
  • A degree in engineering, business, or a related discipline; an MBA or advanced degree is preferred.
  • Identifies opportunities to apply AI for continuous improvement and innovation.

Leadership Profile:

  • An enterprise-minded and progressive thinker with a global perspective.
  • Commercially astute, financially disciplined, and oriented toward growth.
  • Decisive and accountable, with a strong bias for action.
  • Skilled at integrating customer, operational, technical, and market perspectives.
  • A credible executive presence who can influence, motivate, and build lasting relationships.
  • Energized by transformation, complexity, and the opportunity to deliver meaningful outcomes.

It is a requirement that General Dynamics Mission Systems-Canada be registered with the Canadian Controlled Goods program and that all of its workforce be security assessed. Successful applicants must meet all applicable security requirements, including but not limited to the ability to obtain and maintain a Canadian government security clearance. Applicants may be required to meet additional security requirements in order to gain access to technical data, classified areas or information that is subject to international regulations. You must be eligible to work in Canada.

The position offers a competitive base salary and performance-based bonus opportunity, reflecting the seniority, scope and impact of the role.

Benefits
As a full-time employee at General Dynamics Mission Systems–Canada, you’ll enjoy a competitive total rewards package that supports your professional and personal well-being:

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and eligible dependents from day one (no cost), including flexible benefits options (HCSA) emergency travel insurance, and 24/7 virtual care services.
  • Employee & Family Assistance Program (EFAP), onsite fitness facilities, and employee resource groups.
  • Defined Contribution Pension Plan with employer contributions after 3 months, RRSP access from day one, and financial planning support.
  • Flexible time off including vacation, holidays, parental leaves with top-up options, sick leave, and disability programs.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer, CI/CD Platform (Developer Experience)
description:
Hey there, Kubernetes people!

Every engineer here waits on CI several times a day. We want someone who finds that wait personally annoying.

Why this role exists?

Hundreds of developers push to a large Ruby on Rails monorepo, and every push lands on a runner fleet that the Developer Experience team builds, runs and keeps fast.

That fleet is self-hosted Kubernetes on bare metal in European datacentres, in the low hundreds of machines, running eternal GitHub Actions runners that peak above a thousand concurrent pods. We own all of it: the hardware, the clusters, the runner images, the caches and the delivery pipelines on top. We add nodes by hand rather than letting an autoscaler do it, so capacity planning is genuinely part of the job.

The leverage is unusual. Shave a minute off the average build and every engineer in the company gets that minute back, several times a day.

The mission

  • Own the CI and CD Kubernetes clusters end to end: capacity, reliability, upgrades, security and cost.
  • Run the self-hosted GitHub Actions platform at scale with Actions Runner Controller. Runner scale sets, ephemer pods, docker-in-docker, and the runner images themselves.
  • Keep the data services our tests depend on fast and healthy. MySQL, Redis and ClickHouse come up per job, alongside Rails application containers.
  • Design and tune the caching that makes builds quick: node-local overlay, image and artifact caches we build ourselves, plus pull-through registry mirrors.
  • Bring queue wait and build duration down, with measurement behind it. Instrument the platform, set targets, and show the improvement.
  • Manage it all as code. Terraform planned and applied from pull requests, GitOps delivery with Flux and Argo CD, Kustomize and Helm for manifests.
  • Provision and operate bare metal. Linux, networking across datacentre segments, and troubleshooting that sometimes ends up at the disk or the kernel.
  • Lead incident response for the platform, run blameless postmortems, and turn each one into an alert, a guardrail or a runbook.
  • Treat the platform as a product whose users are engineers. Talk to them, watch where they get stuck, and build paths that make the right thing easy.

Your day to day

  • Rightsizing runner tiers against a week of CPU and memory data, then opening the pull request that changes them.
  • Tracking a flaky job from a red check down to the container runtime, the kernel, or a clock that drifted.
  • Adding machines to the fleet: install, enrol, network, verify, document.
  • Cutting p95 queue wait by working out which stage actually blocks.
  • Upgrading a cluster or a controller without anyone noticing.
  • Pairing with a product engineer on a workflow that has been slow for a reason nobody has looked at yet.

Your profile

  • 5+ years running production infrastructure, with Kubernetes at the centre of it.
  • Real depth in Kubernetes: scheduling, requests and limits, evictions, node pressure, DaemonSets, controllers and operators. You have debugged a cluster that was lying to you.
  • Strong Linux and container fundamentals. containerd or Docker internals, cgroups, namespaces, storage drivers, networking.
  • Terraform and infrastructure as code, with a feel for module design and state hygiene.
  • CI/CD at the platform level: shared workflows, reusable templates, runner architecture, build caching.
  • Comfortable with GitHub Actions, including self-hosted runners.
  • You script to automate. Bash, plus at least one of Python or Go.
  • Observability as a working method. Metrics, logs, traces, dashboards and alerts that people trust, with OpenTelemetry and Prometheus style tooling.
  • Operational maturity. On-call, incident command, postmortems, and the discipline to chase causes.
  • Capacity and cost awareness. You can size a fleet and explain the bill.
  • Clear written English. You document what you built, because the next person on call will not be you.

Bonus points

  • Large Ruby on Rails test suites, and what it takes to parallelise them honestly.
  • Operating MySQL, Redis or ClickHouse yourself.
  • Bare metal: provisioning, hardware failure, and the different rhythm it has compared to cloud.
  • Overlay and WireGuard style mesh networking, VLANs, and Kubernetes CNIs such as Cilium.
  • Building internal developer tooling, portals or platform APIs.
  • Supply chain and build security. Runner isolation, secret scoping, image provenance.
  • Working across more than one cloud. We use AWS, Azure and Cloudflare alongside our own hardware.
  • Contributions to open source infrastructure projects.

How we work

At Factorial, we believe the best products are built when people come together, in person, to collaborate, challenge ideas, and move fast. That’s why our Engineering Team follows an office-first, flexible approach.

We work on-site several days a week (80%), using that time to connect, align, and innovate as a team. However, we also support remote work when it makes sense (20%) for deep focus or personal needs.

At Factorial we don't evaluate you by years of experience but by your knowledge and skills.

We use our Career Path with a rubric framework where we define what is expected for each experience level and skill. This framework allows you to know your current level and what you need to keep growing. We love transparency, so our Career Path includes the salaries for each level, which we share during the first interview to ensure alignment.

Our Hiring Process

  • Intro Call: Chat with our Talent Partner about your journey and goals.
  • Hiring Manager Interview: Deep dive into your product mindset, teamwork, and problem-solving.
  • Technical Interview: A collaborative technical conversation with the team based on real-life problems.
  • Final Coffee Chat: A relaxed conversation with our CTO & VP of Engineering to explore our vision, culture, and your growth.

And that’s it! Feel free to request any other conversations you want, with team members or to address specific concerns at any time in the process. The whole process is remote, using videoconferencing tools!

Company culture

We believe in diverse talent: we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and strongly encourage people of diverse experiences and identities to apply.

We believe in inclusion: we are committed to equal opportunities and actively promote workplace inclusion of people with disabilities. If you would like to learn more about our inclusive recruitment processes, you are welcome to indicate so optionally and we will share additional information with you.

Perks of being part of Factorial

  • High growth, multicultural and friendly environment
  • Alan as private health insurance
  • Healthy life with Wellhub (Gyms, pools, outdoor classes)
  • Save expenses with Cobee
  • Language classes
  • Breakfast in the office and organic fruit
  • Food discounts with Nora
  • Pet Friendly
  • Much more that we'll spill during the interview process!

About Factorial

At Factorial, we’re building the leading AI Business Management Software for companies of all sizes. Our platform centralizes key workflows across HR, Finance, Talent, Operations, and IT, freeing teams from manual processes so they can focus on what really matters: leading, growing, and taking care of their people. With over 1,500 employees across Europe, Asia, Africa, and America. We are one of Europe’s fastest-growing SaaS companies, proudly headquartered in Barcelona. If you're excited to shape the future of business management technology, we’d love to meet you.

Wanna learn more about us? Check our website!

The primary functions of the Production Lead include but are not limited to assisting in managing the performance of day-to-day operational activities which may include pit and/or plant production (primary, secondary, chip plant, wash plant, etc.) The Lead also assists in training and developing a safe and efficient hourly workforce through use of the company’s safety policies and procedures, MSHA and other regulations, continuous improvement, meeting production and costs goals, quality control and other functions as assigned by management. This individual will work night shift Monday-Friday (6pm-6am).

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES/ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Ensure the crushing and screening plant operates safely, efficiently, and within all quality specifications.
  • Proficient and safe operation of all plant crushing, screening & conveyor systems.
  • Ensure that all hourly employees under his/her area of responsibility receive competent task training to safely perform his/her job duties and that such training is properly documented in a timely manner.
  • Assist in managing all daily activities of all hourly production and support personnel.
  • Conduct regular site inspections to ensure all safety, maintenance, and plant cleanup items are addressed correctly and in a timely manner.
  • Assist management with all daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly reporting requirements.
  • Ensure that all plant equipment on site is properly maintained according to Dolese Bros. Co. maintenance program requirements.
  • Ability and knowledge to operate and monitor equipment in a safe and efficient manner.
  • Ability to perform preventive maintenance and pre-shift inspections; repair and/or clean equipment as needed.
  • Ability to comprehend and complete all needed paperwork in a timely and accurate manner.
  • Regular, reliable attendance at the worksite or assigned work location.
  • Identify, communicate, plan, lead, and execute plant performance improvement projects.
  • Troubleshoot issues that arise with crushers, screens and conveyors and collaborate with reliability and maintenance staff to remedy the problem.
  • Perform workplace exams identifying problems that might affect future plant availability and performance.
  • Communicate effectively with Plant Operations Technician to start, stop, maintain, and troubleshoot plant equipment.
  • Intimately understand plant flow and mechanical equipment operation to optimize daily production.
  • Build effective relationships with plant support personnel to rally and lead resources during downtime or upset plant conditions.
  • Promote and maintain a culture and attitude of continual improvement, working & leading within the Dolese team to make it more efficient, safer and an enjoyable place to work.
  • Identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Coordinate with reliability & maintenance team to fix issues that arise with the plant.
  • Address root cause issues that regularly cause cleanup throughout plant.
  • Ability to read, write and comprehend reports including but not limited to: safety inspections, production reporting and maintenance records.

title: Senior Backend Developer - Madrid
description:
The team that makes our magic work is growing: will you be a part of it?

Company Description:

Fidesmo is a leading technology company based in Stockholm with a research and development center in Madrid. We are building a platform to distribute contactless services to any device having a secure chip: in other words, we want that any watch, bracelet, ring, piece of clothing or even subcutaneous implant (yes, you read right) can be used to pay for a purchase, hop on the train, get inside an office building or rent a car. Our most successful service is Fidesmo Pay, launched together with Visa, Mastercard, banks and a select group of manufacturers of wearable devices: for example, we are the ones powering Swatch Pay and the payments solution in Honor latest smartwatches.

This requires writing code that runs on a chip with only a few kilobytes of RAM, or very scalable server code, or clients for the main environments (iOS, Android, web and also command line). By building our own product we are free from the typical pressure coming from contract development: we program with quality following our own rules.

Role Description:

You will be part of the backend team, building the services that connect to payment networks, public transportation authorities, etc, and also to secure chips on devices. You will extend our microservices architecture, understand and modify our data model, ensuring performance, reliability and maintainability.

We follow an Agile methodology for software development; you will participate in design and implementation decisions and contribute to planning and code reviews. You will participate and improve the continuous integration and devops processes.

We expect that you will lead development projects, participating in requirements discussions with other teams in the company and also with external partners. You will contribute with your experience and help less experienced developers, while also learning domain-specific tools and standards.

We welcome developers who are willing to experiment with new technologies, prototype and use what works best. Fidesmo will train you in the specific programming languages, cryptography and other domain knowledge necessary for the job.

Qualifications

  • 3–5 years professional experience building server-side applications
  • REST API design experience; able to make and defend architecture decisions
  • Experience writing/maintaining unit, functional, and integration tests
  • Experience gathering requirements and working with external partners/customers
  • Deep knowledge of Java, Kotlin, or Scala
  • Enjoys collaborative, small-team work with mutual code review
  • Comfortable working in English day-to-day

Nice to have

  • Functional programming experience
  • Docker/containerization, CI tooling, event-based architectures, logging/monitoring
  • Cryptography and key management experience

What's offered

  • Onboarding with formal + on-the-job training alongside experienced developers
  • Central Madrid office, well connected by Cercanías/Metro/bus
  • Flexible hours and remote work
  • Restaurant tickets
  • 25 days annual paid vacation

title: Account Payable Administrator
description:
Employment Status:

Regular

Time Type:

Full time

BUILDING A WORLD CLASS TEAM STARTS WITH YOU

At the heart of CSA Group is a vision: making the world a better, safer, more sustainable place. It's been part of our mission for nearly one hundred years: from the first engineering standard for railway bridges developed in 1919, to more than 3,500 standards, codes & related products today.

Headquartered in Canada, with a global footprint of more than 30 labs and offices across Europe, Asia and North America, CSA Group tests, inspects and certifies a wide range of products - from every day househould items to leading edge technology-to meet exacting requirements for safety, performance and environmental impact.

Our employees take pride in making a difference in people's lives through the work that we do. We're looking for people like you to help make it happen.

Job Summary:

PRIMARY FUNCTION

Works within the core accounting team, under the Canadian Standards Association’s Finance Function.

Primary function is to perform:

  • Vendor invoice processing;

  • Cash settlement transactions (including vendor payments and transfers of cash); and

  • Addressing accounts payable and vendor payment matters

PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Responsible for daily preparation, verification and inputting of approved invoices into SAP/Workday AP module. Approved invoices consist of vendor invoices associated with purchase orders, vendor invoices without purchase orders, employee travel expense reports and refunds to accounts receivable customers.

  • Responsible for ensuring vendor invoices for services extending over a period of time or for goods not yet delivered are set up as prepaid expenses and the respective amortization schedule is created.

  • Responsible for proper selection of invoices for weekly or bi-weekly payment and the subsequent payment and distribution through one of the following methods: cheque, Bill Pay (web service) RBC/BofA EFTs and Wires. Responsible for selection of appropriate bank account from which payments are to be made (depending on payment currency, paying legal entity, etc.).

  • Responsible for logging and maintaining a summary sheet for cheque printing control which is reviewed and signed off by management (Standards only). Ensures proper backup is attached for all payments/cheques in excess of $20,000 that are forwarded to management personnel for approval.

  • Responsible for data transferred from concur to workday/SAP successfully, including employee Concur travel/P-card entries. Inform related parties for any issue/errors.

  • Responsible for having knowledge of and ensuring compliance with Finance policies and procedures affecting the accounts payable and cash settlement functions and others relevant.

  • Addresses Canadian Standards Association vendor enquiries, following up with the vendor and Canadian Standards Association personnel in Procurement and other departments, as required.

  • Expected to assist external auditors and PST/HST auditors in the retrieving and explaining of paid vendor invoices.

  • Responsible for entering journal entries (parked documents) in SAP and Record Ad Hoc Bank Transactions in Workday (Cash Journal Entries), as required.

  • Responsible for reviewing, analyzing, investigating and resolving items in the GR/IR account which do not clear promptly (only for SAP.

  • Responsible for providing a weekly forecast of cash requirements to the Treasury function and to assist with Cash Management. Purchase/Sell/transfer funds as needed to support account balances on a weekly basis in RBC and BOFA to facilitate these cash needs.

  • Responsible for informing Finance Manager of large amounts that need to be accrued on a monthly basis (based on knowledge of large invoices not entered at Month-end)

  • Responsible for obtaining a list of cleared cheques through RBC and performs on-line clearing on a daily basis (SAP only). Liaises with bank staff on legitimacy of cheques processed through RBC. Expected to be vigilant of signs of cheque fraud. Prepares and verifies bank deposit for U.S. and Cdn. Cheques on a daily basis.

  • Responsible for properly maintaining the accounting records according to Canadian Standards Association policies and procedures which include but are not limited to monetary transactions, supplier invoices, SAP vendor change form, supporting docs e.g. cheques, approvals etc.

  • Support the general accounting and reporting team with analysis and reporting activities

  • From time to time, will assist the Finance Manager and other departments with ad-hoc projects and activities on an as-needed basis.

WORKING RELATIONSHIPS

  • Reports to Finance Manager or equivalent.

  • Works with and communicates with external vendors, banks and Canadian Standards Association personnel, as required.

DIMENSIONS

  • Participates in the Canadian Standards Associations incentive targets.

  • Responsible for ensuring the Workday/SAP/Email inbox is cleared on a timely basis and maintained current.

  • Responsible for ensuring the AP inbox/AP drive containing vendor invoices is actioned on a daily basis and maintained current.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Expected to work from the office based on the schedule as agreed with team and within Company guidelines and policies and utilize tools provided (phone, personal computer with extended screen)

  • Expected to work past normal working hours on occasion with rest of Finance team (i.e. in preparation for and during annual financial statement audit [March through May] and occasionally at Month-end).

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Post-secondary education, preferably Accounting or Finance related

  • A minimum of 2 years of related experience

  • Requires working knowledge of one or more of the following computer applications: SAP (AP, GL, AR), Workday, BOFA, Bill Pay (web service) RBC, and Concur.

As per the collective agreement, the starting bi-weekly pay rate for an Accounts Payable Administrator is $2,346.20 CAD gross. CSA Group reserves the right to determine the appropriate level and pay step within the band, and this will depend on factors such as education, licenses, certifications and experience. As part of our total rewards offering, permanent employees in this position may be eligible for our annual bonus program, subject to program eligibility requirements.

CSA Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on any grounds stipulated by applicable laws. We are an organization where opportunities are based on skills and abilities, and differences are respected and valued. Please contact us at talentacquisition@csagroup.org if you require accommodation in the interview process.

title: Account Lead - Convenience
description:

Why You Should Join Us

At Molson Coors, we've been bringing people together over a cold beer for more than 200 years. Our award-winning portfolio includes beloved brands such as Cobra, Coors, Carling, Madri Excepcional and Blue Moon, our diverse range also features popular brands like Aspall, Rekorderlig, Staropramen, and Doom Bar.

About The Role

We're looking for a commercially driven Account Lead to join our Convenience team and play a pivotal role in delivering growth across one of our most important channels.

This is more than a customer management role. You'll be responsible for leading a cross-functional team, shaping customer strategy, influencing senior stakeholders, and driving outstanding commercial performance. If you thrive on building winning partnerships, negotiating complex agreements, and developing people, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Be Doing

As Account Lead, you'll own the day-to-day customer relationship and lead a Multi-Functional Selling Team (MFST) to deliver ambitious growth plans.

You'll:

  • Take full accountability for delivering sales, profit and commercial objectives across your customer portfolio.
  • Build and strengthen strategic relationships with senior customer stakeholders, including Buying Managers and wider decision-makers.
  • Identify and unlock new commercial opportunities that drive sustainable growth for both customer and business.
  • Lead customer planning, execution and performance management across monthly, quarterly and annual business cycles.
  • Inspire and coordinate a cross-functional team, ensuring everyone is aligned behind shared objectives and customer priorities.
  • Deliver against key commercial metrics including volume, net sales revenue, forecast accuracy and customer satisfaction measures.
  • Partner closely with the Customer Director to shape and execute both short and long-term customer strategies.
  • Coach, develop and support team members to help them reach their full potential and accelerate their careers.

About You

  • You'll be an experienced FMCG sales professional with a track record of delivering results in a fast-paced commercial environment.
  • You’ll have significant FMCG commercial experience, ideally working with major retail or convenience customers.
  • You’ll have proven success delivering Annual Operating Plans (AOP) and long-term growth strategies.
  • You’ll have well developed negotiation and influencing skills, with experience engaging senior internal and external stakeholders.
  • You’ll be able to demonstrate the ability to identify growth opportunities and convert them into commercial results.
  • You’ll have experience leading complex customer conversations and negotiations with confidence.

We know not everyone will meet every requirement. If you’re excited about this role and believe you can make a difference, we’d love to hear from you.

About Us

  • We’re one of the UK’s Most Attractive Employers winning the Top Employer award for the last 13 years.
  • Flexible work programmes to ensure a work life balance is maintained such as our market leading Moments That Matter for significant moments in your life.
  • Commitment to the physical and mental wellbeing of all our people reflective of our People First value.
  • We’re committed to raising industry standards and leaving a positive imprint on our employees, consumers, communities, and the environment.

Molson Coors; Brands to Love, Careers to Last

Molson Coors Beverage Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and we seek, value and respect everyone’s unique perspectives and experiences knowing that we are stronger together.

Our aim to build a skilled and highly engaged workforce that unites around our shared values and reflects our diverse marketplace; and​ foster a workplace where all employees’ unique talents, skills and perspectives are valued and leveraged – where all people feel that we are #BetterWithYou.​ This makes our talent strategy simple – we want the best talent in all our roles, regardless of their background.

We are Disability Confident Committed. If you require any additional assistance or adjustments in advance of, or during the application and/or hiring process, please contact us at careers@molsoncoors.com.​

We want you to succeed and will be happy to support you.

Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal prompting.

Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. We believe products will greatly reduce hallucinations

Our objective is to organise anyone's life, allowing us all to spend time on valuable and meaningful things

Role

As an Android Developer, AI Apps, you own the Android client experience, how AI feels, behaves, and performs on mobile devices. This is not a thin client role. You will build a production Android application where AI interactions are core to the product, and performance, reliability, and clarity matter.

Focus

  • Build and maintain production Android apps using Kotlin.
  • Integrate AI-powered features (chat, vision, voice, recommendations) via backend APIs.

  • Ensure app stability, security, and scalability in production environments.

Ideal Experiences

  • 3+ years of Android development experience using Kotlin.
  • Hands-on experience integrating AI features (e.g. LLM, vision, speech APIs).
  • Strong understanding of asynchronous programming (Coroutines, Flow).
  • Familiarity with REST or gRPC APIs and structured data formats.
  • Strong debugging and performance profiling skills.
  • Comfort building in environments with latency, partial failure, and non-deterministic behavior.
  • Experience with MLKit or light on-device inference.
  • Published production apps on the Google Play Store.

Outcomes

  • Stable, smooth, and reliable real-world use android applications.

  • Kotlin / Java

How We Work

The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands‑on team. Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment, and execute independently. Our goal is to put in hands of our users a truly magical product

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach to schedule 3, but no more than 4 interviews.

Applications are evaluated by our technical team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite.

We value transparency and efficiency, so expect a prompt decision. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us. This isn't just a job offer; it's an invitation to be part of a team that's bringing AI to have practical benefits to billions globally.

title: Change Management & Business Adoption Lead
location: United States - New York - New York City
description:
Use Your Power For Purpose

As the Change Management & Business Adoption Lead, you will drive a culture of change agility across GBM. This role leads the integration of change adoption and strategy so that new tools and processes are not only defined—but understood, adopted, and continuously improved across a global network.


What You Will Achieve

  • Leading end-to-end change management for GBM transformation initiatives and business processes, this includes impact assessments, stakeholder analysis, change strategy development, communication planning, capability building, and reinforcement mechanisms to ensure sustainable adoption of new processes, systems, and behaviors.
  • Monitoring adoption of transformation activities and adjusting change management approaches to ensure progress.
  • Designing and directing systems that capture, organize, and share project knowledge to improve decision-making, compliance, and operational efficiency to sustain new business program, approaches and processes.
  • Leading the development and execution of stakeholder engagement strategies, communication plans (global + site-level), and knowledge management and capability-building programs.
  • Providing coaching to leaders and teams on leading through change, embedding new behaviors and leveraging new systems, processes and tools effectively.
  • Leading or supporting the design and implementation of transformation initiatives in processes, ensuring alignment with regulatory expectations, data integrity principles, and business value objectives.
  • Partnering with leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to assess readiness, manage impacts, and drive sustainable adoption of transformation initiatives.
  • Benchmarking internally and externally to identify best practices and integrate relevant learnings into processes, systems, and ways of working.
  • Monitoring change adoption through KPIs, feedback loops, and behavioral insights, and adjust strategies accordingly.

ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES

Focus Areas

  • Change Management:
    • Define and lead the change management strategy for GBM Transformation initiatives, including new processes, system enhancements, policy updates, organizational changes, and AI/digital and continuous improvement programs.
    • Partner with team members, global leaders, sites, and markets to ensure changes are implemented consistently while allowing for appropriate local deployment considerations.
    • Assess change saturation, risk, and organizational readiness to reduce disruption and improve adoption.
  • Stakeholder Engagement, Communications & Adoption
    • Lead stakeholder mapping, change impact assessments, and engagement strategies for global and site-level audiences.
    • Develop communication plans tailored to executive leaders, process owners, site teams, manufacturing colleagues, and other impacted users.
    • Translate changes into clear, practical, globally understandable messaging.
    • Create adoption strategies that go beyond awareness, focusing on behavior change, role clarity, capability building, and sustained process performance.
    • Partner with AI Acceleration/Transformation Office and FRAME PWOW and other teams to ensure project knowledge is accessible, current, controlled, and aligned.
    • Establish feedback loops with sites, functions, and end users to identify adoption barriers and improvement opportunities.
    • Identify systemic barriers to adoption and recommend improvements to governance, communication, documentation, or training approaches.

Here Is What You Need (Minimum Requirements)

  • Bachelor's degree with at least 8 years of experience; OR a master's degree with at least 5 years of experience
  • Demonstrated experience leading change management for complex transformation initiatives, including stakeholder engagement, organizational readiness assessment, communication strategy, capability development, and sustainment in regulated environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence, collaborate, and drive alignment across global, cross-functional, and matrixed organizations, including engagement with senior stakeholders; anticipating and leading others through ambiguity by continuously creating context and engaging individuals in what it means for them.
  • Significant experience in the pharmaceutical or life sciences industry, including substantial exposure to quality, compliance, inspection readiness, and/or operational excellence within regulated environments.
  • Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional transformation initiatives with measurable impact in regulated environments, including the ability to translate strategy into execution and sustainable outcomes.
  • Experience developing and utilizing metrics / KPI reporting and governance frameworks to monitor performance, drive accountability, and enable data-driven decision-making.
  • Strong program and project management capabilities, including experience managing multiple initiatives, prioritizing workload, and driving execution through structured governance routines.
  • Demonstrated innovation, flexibility, open-mindedness, and adaptability to meet objectives in a rapidly changing environment with shifting priorities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience supporting transformations, IMEx, digital, or process standardization.
  • Experience working across global manufacturing sites or matrixed organizations.
  • Experience applying continuous improvement methodologies (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma, DMAIC, IMEx, OPEX) to drive measurable process simplification, efficiency gains, and sustainable compliance improvements.
  • Experience driving business transformation, PMO, or governance models, including portfolio management, milestone tracking, performance reporting, and cross-functional execution discipline.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and operate effectively across diverse, global, and matrixed organizations.

title: Senior B2B Insights Consultant DACH (m/f/d)
description:
Allow us to introduce ourselves

Hello there! We’re Appinio, a global market research company that combines an AI-powered insights platform with expert consultancy. On a mission to make the world a little more fact-based, we help companies understand how consumers think and make smarter decisions.

We started out in Hamburg back in 2014, but we’re now humbled to call the world our playground, with over 260 employees spread across 13 countries (we’re remote-first), 2600+ international clients, delivering research from +190 markets, globally.

Want to be a part of the Appinio movement? 🚀

Here at Appinio, we value transparency in our recruitment process, and we've created a blog to share what to expect during each step of our journey together: here

Your mission as a Senior Research Consultant

We are looking for a Senior Research Consultant (m/f/d) with a strong quantitative market research background to join our newly dedicated B2B research team in the DACH region. This specialized unit focuses on research projects that specifically survey B2B target groups, professional decision-makers, and niche business audiences (rather than only standard B2C consumer panels), serving fast-moving consultancy clients and corporate B2B requests.

In this role, you will lead complex quantitative B2B research projects end-to-end, from initial feasibility alignment and study design to reporting and insight presentation. You will act as a senior sparring partner for corporate strategy leads and consultancy teams, translating intricate B2B & B2C data into clear, decision-ready recommendations. You will thrive in a high-velocity environment where speed, rigorous B2B screening logic, strong client presence, and operational precision are essential.

What you’ll be doing

  • End-to-End B2B Project Lead: Manage quantitative research projects end-to-end, including B2B screening design, questionnaire drafting, platform setup, fieldwork monitoring, and data delivery.
  • Methodology & Study Design: Optimise bespoke study designs across core use cases (e.g., Target Group Analysis, U&A, Pricing studies, Concept Testing) mainly tailored to hard-to-reach professional audiences.
  • Senior Client Sparring & Advisory: Act as a trusted partner for fast-paced consultancy and corporate clients, advising on sample feasibility, survey logic, and optimal research approaches under tight deadlines.
  • Commercial & Scoping Collaboration: Partner closely with Sales and Account Management on project scoping, feasibility checks, and methodology definition for complex project requests.
  • Process & Quality Enhancement: Contribute to standardizing B2B screening protocols, sampling frameworks, and best practices to coach other researcher and safeguard delivery speed and research quality across the team.

You will thrive in this role if

  • You have 5+ years of experience in quantitative market research with a distinct focus on surveying B2B target groups and professional decision-makers (agency or consulting background required; pure academic or non-client backgrounds will not fit this role).
  • You have hands-on experience designing studies, writing questionnaires, and executing quantitative projects across core B2B use cases (e.g., U&A, Pricing studies, Concept Testing, Target Group Analysis).
  • You bring proven experience creating executive-ready reports and presenting complex data through clear, compelling storytelling to senior client-side stakeholders.
  • You possess a strategic, commercially minded approach with the self-confidence to guide clients and defend research decisions under pressure.
  • You excel in high-velocity environments, with a demonstrated ability to juggle multiple concurrent projects, prioritize effectively, and stay calm under tight deadlines.
  • You are proficient in German (C2 level required) and English, with outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
  • You bring a pragmatic, proactive, and resilient mindset with a passion for data quality and innovation.

What’s in it for you?

  • Flexibility Policy - Our flexibility policy means there is no hard cap on the number of vacation days you can take
  • Temporary work from abroad - If you're based in the EU, you can work outside your country of residence for up to 180 days per year
  • All the hardware you need and your own MacBook
  • If you are located in Hamburg or Berlin, you'll get a Deutschland ticket or access to a mobility budget with the NAVIT app to get you to and from the office space
  • Subsidised Urban Sports Club or ClassPass membership based on location
  • In case you’re located in one of the cities where most of our fellow Appinioneers are (Hamburg, Berlin, Munich, London, Madrid, Barcelona, or New York), you can get access to our Co-working spaces

Kind reminder: Please ensure that your application is submitted in English.

title: National Fellowships Program Coordinator
description:
Job Title

National Fellowships Program Coordinator

Agency

Texas A&M University

Department

National Fellowships

Proposed Minimum Salary

$32.05 hourly

Job Location

College Station, Texas

Job Type

Staff

Job Description

What We Want

The Office of National Fellowships is seeking a Program Coordinator I to support outreach and the coordination of national fellowship and internal award opportunities at Texas A&M University. We are looking for an organized, proactive, and student-centered professional who will play a key role in coordinating campus fellowship competitions, supporting students throughout the application process, maintaining accurate program information and records, and expanding awareness of national fellowship opportunities across the university.

The successful candidate will serve as an important point of contact for students, faculty, campus committee members, and university partners. This individual will coordinate campus review processes, manage application timelines and materials, maintain the Office’s website and fellowship database, support outreach initiatives (including through social media), and conduct advising appointments with students interested in national fellowships.

We are looking for someone who is highly organized and detail-oriented, able to manage multiple deadlines simultaneously, and comfortable working with sensitive student information. The ideal candidate will be able to learn and communicate complex eligibility requirements, application procedures, and fellowship expectations clearly to a variety of audiences. Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, problem-solving abilities, and proficiency in Excel and Google Forms is essential.

The successful candidate will be comfortable working independently while also collaborating with students, faculty, staff, and campus partners. Experience working in higher education, particularly in academic advising, student development, study abroad, undergraduate research, honors programs, scholarships, fellowships, or academic writing support will be especially valuable.

If you are excited about helping students identify and pursue transformative national fellowship opportunities while contributing to the growth of a university-wide program, we encourage you to apply.

What You Need to Know

Salary: $32.05/hourly (Based on selected hire’s qualifications).

Cover Letter & Resume: A cover letter and resume are strongly recommended.

Position Details:

  • This will be a part time benefits eligible position. Expected to work 24 hours per week.

  • Includes occasional evening or weekend hours to support events, programs, and fellowship deadlines.

Qualifications

Required Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in any field.

  • At least two years of experience in academic advising, undergraduate research or honors programs, study abroad, higher education administration, scholarship or fellowship administration, or writing center.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in any field.

  • Experience working in undergraduate research, honors program, or other student support programs.

  • Experience working with national fellowships, scholarships, grants, or other competitive academic opportunities.

  • Experience advising or mentoring students.

  • Experience coordinating faculty or university committees.

  • Experience maintaining websites, databases, student information systems, or other digital information platforms.

  • Experience developing outreach, recruitment, or communications initiatives for students, including through social media.

  • Familiarity with national fellowship programs and/or competitive scholarship opportunities.

  • International experience, study abroad experience, or experience working with internationally focused programs.

  • Experience using university systems for student records, appointment scheduling, event management, communications, or data management.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Ability to work in person in an office environment.

  • Ability to work at a computer for extended periods of time.

  • Ability to work occasional evening or weekend hours to support events, programs, and application deadlines.

  • Ability to work independently and take initiative while also collaborating effectively as part of a team.

  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, and priorities simultaneously.

  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate records and application information.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate professionally with students, faculty, staff, and external stakeholders.

  • Ability to learn and communicate complex eligibility requirements, application procedures, and program guidelines.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including experience working with Excel spreadsheet and Google Forms.

  • Experience advising students in a professional setting.

  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment when handling student records, applications, and other sensitive information.

  • Ability to coordinate meetings, events, committees, and other activities involving multiple participants and competing schedules

Essential Duties/Tasks

  • Campus Fellowship and Internal Award Competition and Committee Coordination - Coordinates campus application and review processes for national fellowship and internal award competitions requiring university nomination or campus review. Responsibilities include maintaining fellowship timelines, coordinating campus deadlines, collecting and organizing application materials, communicating requirements to applicants, recruiting and coordinating campus committee members, scheduling committee meetings and interviews, preparing committee materials and rubrics, distributing applications and supporting documents, tracking committee feedback and decisions, and communicating outcomes and next steps to students and campus partners. Maintains accurate records of campus competitions and develops systems and processes to ensure that deadlines, committee requirements, applicant information, and follow-up activities are consistently tracked. Supports the development and improvement of campus review procedures and assists with special projects related to the administration of national fellowship competitions.

  • Program Operations, Website, and Database Management - Supports the daily operations of the Office of National Fellowships and serves as a central source of administrative support for the program. Maintains accurate fellowship information, deadlines, eligibility requirements, application procedures, and program descriptions in the Office’s database and online resources. Maintains and updates the Office website and other digital resources to ensure that information is accurate, current, accessible, and presented clearly to students, faculty, and campus partners. Maintains student and fellowship records, spreadsheets, tracking systems, and other databases used to administer programs and assess student engagement. Assists with data collection, reporting, assessment, and preparation of materials for internal and external audiences. Identifies inconsistencies or outdated information and proactively works to correct records and improve information-management processes.

  • Student Advising and Application Support - Provides individual and group advising support to students interested in national fellowships and scholarships. Responds to student inquiries, conducts advising appointments, explains fellowship eligibility requirements and application processes, and helps students understand campus and external deadlines. Supports students in identifying appropriate fellowship opportunities and navigating application requirements. Provides general guidance on application components, timelines, and campus processes while referring students to appropriate faculty, staff, or external resources when specialized assistance is needed. Assists with developing and delivering workshops, information sessions, presentations, and other educational programming designed to introduce students to national fellowship opportunities and strengthen their understanding of the application process.

  • Outreach, Recruitment, and Communications - Supports outreach initiatives designed to increase awareness and participation in national fellowship opportunities across Texas A&M University. Collaborates with colleges, departments, academic programs, student organizations, faculty, advisors, and other campus partners to promote fellowship opportunities and identify prospective applicants. Assists with planning and implementing information sessions, presentations, workshops, tabling activities, outreach campaigns, and other recruitment initiatives. Develops and maintains communications materials, including emails, presentations, handouts, website content, social media content, and other promotional materials. Responds to inquiries from students, faculty, staff, and campus partners in a timely and professional manner and helps ensure consistent communication about fellowship opportunities, deadlines, and program procedures.

  • Administrative Support, Assessment, and Professional Development - Maintains office calendars, files, records, and administrative documentation. Assists with event logistics, purchasing, reimbursements, supplies, meeting preparation, and other administrative functions that support the daily operations of the Office of National Fellowships. Collects and maintains program participation and outcome data and assists with assessment activities designed to evaluate and improve Office programs and services. Participates in team meetings and contributes to the development and improvement of office procedures, resources, and systems. Engages in ongoing professional development related to national fellowships, student advising, higher education administration, and other areas relevant to the position. Performs other duties as assigned to support the Office of National Fellowships.

Who We Are

The Office of National Fellowships supports high-achieving and purpose-driven students as they pursue nationally and internationally competitive awards. We help students discover their potential, articulate their aspirations, and develop the skills needed to compete for prestigious opportunities that expand their academic, professional, and global engagement.

Why Texas A&M University?

We are a prestigious university with strong traditions, Core Values, and a community of caring and collaboration. Amenities associated with a major university, such as sporting and cultural events, state-of-the-art recreation facilities, the Bush Library and Museum, and much more await you. Experience all that a big city has to offer but with a reasonable cost-of-living and no long commutes.

  • Living Well, a program at Texas A&M that has been built by employees, for employees

Our Commitment

Texas A&M University is committed to enriching the learning and working environment by promoting a culture that respects all perspectives, talents & lived experience. Embracing varying opinions and perspectives strengthens our core values which are: Respect, Excellence, Leadership, Loyalty, Integrity, and Selfless Service.

description:

As a Software Engineering Intern within the Apple Ads team, you will contribute to the design, development, and optimization of our advertising platforms, with a particular focus on leveraging machine learning to enhance ad relevance, forecasting, performance, and user experience. You will work alongside experienced engineers on challenging projects, gaining hands-on experience with large-scale data, machine learning models, and distributed systems. Responsibilities may include developing and deploying machine learning algorithms, analyzing data to identify insights, writing clean and efficient code for production systems, participating in code reviews, debugging issues, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality, privacy-preserving advertising solutions.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Machine Learning, Data Science, or a related technical field.
  • Strong foundational knowledge in data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented programming.
  • Proficiency in at least one programming language commonly used in machine learning or backend development (e.g., Python, Java, Scala, C++).
  • Familiarity with version control systems (e.g., Git).
  • Knowledge of database systems (SQL/NoSQL) and data warehousing concepts.
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills, with an ability to analyze complex data.
  • Understanding of fundamental machine learning concepts and statistical methods, with experience using machine learning frameworks and libraries (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch, scikit-learn).
  • Exposure to model optimization techniques such as quantization, tensor parallelism, and inference optimization (e.g., ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, vLLM).
  • Familiarity with modern neural network architectures (e.g., Transformers, DNNs, RNNs) and training pipelines.
  • Awareness of reinforcement learning, explore/exploit strategies, and bandit-based optimization concepts.
  • Exposure to GenAI and agentic system concepts and their application to machine learning workflows.
  • Familiarity with large-scale data processing technologies (e.g., Spark, Hadoop, Flink) and distributed systems (e.g., Ray, high-throughput RPC systems) to support scalable inference and data workloads.
  • Experience with or exposure to A/B testing infrastructure and performance measurement at scale.
  • Prior coursework or projects related to advertising technology, recommender systems, natural language processing, computer vision, or privacy-preserving ML techniques (e.g., federated learning).
  • Ability to communicate effectively, both written and verbal, with technical and non-technical multi-functional teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with an ability to articulate technical concepts.
  • Demonstrated ability to learn new technologies quickly and adapt to evolving project requirements.

title: National Project Officer (Reception Facility Operations)
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates as well as external women candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

Organizational Context and Scope

Under the direct supervision of the AVRR Coordinator, and the overall supervision of the IOM Head of Programme
and Chief of Mission of IOM Algeria, the incumbent will be responsible for supporting the daily management of the Reception Facility for Voluntary Return (DARV), working closely with the AVRR, Protection, and Operations Units and with IOM partners.

Coordinate the day-to-day running of the Reception Facility for Voluntary Return (DARV), which accommodates
up to 300 migrants per day. Serve as main focal with the main service provider (OPLA) for the maintenance, catering
of the DARV, pre departure activities, distribution of kits, liaising with other IOM partners, and staff scheduling and
rotation, whilst ensuring compliance with IOM standard operating procedures.
2. In coordination with the Information Management Unit and the Field Support staff, monitor MiMOSA cost
management DARV activities and beneficiaries and flag any concern to the IOM Algeria IM Unit.
3. Coordinate with Direct Assistance staff to review and consolidate identified operational needs at the DARV and
follow up with the Procurement and Logistics Unit to ensure timely procurement of goods and services, in line with
IOM procedures.
4. Facilitate accountability towards migrants (AAP) by supporting the establishment and implementation of a
feedback and complaints mechanism, in coordination with the AAP Officer.
5. Contribute to monitoring activities at the DARV by assisting the M&E Unit with data collection and reporting to
support continuous improvement of services.
6. Support external activities taking place at the transit center, acting as focal point in coordination with the
Programme Unit, including preparation for visits by government, donors, and others.
7. Facilitate the participation of migrants in the DARV's governance system, with an emphasis on the meaningful
inclusion of all migrants in decision-making processes in coordination with the AAP and M&E Officers.
8. Support the dissemination, awareness, and observance of the DARV's internal rules, apply disciplinary measures
as instructed, and report any incidents or challenges to the supervisor.
9. Coordinate the referral of migrants with specific needs to the relevant IOM units (e.g. protection, medical,
operations, reintegration), ensuring timely communication and follow-up.
10. Prepare and submit detailed weekly operational reports, highlighting progress, challenges, and suggestions, to
support the proper functioning of the center.
11. Supervise and guide a team of assistants at the center, ensuring effective task distribution, monitoring of their
work performance, and supporting staff well-being, quality of work and compliance with standards.
12. Coordinate the implementation of AVRR procedures for all migrant movements, in close collaboration with the
AVRR Coordinator.
13. Support the implementation of pre-departure activities at the DARV, including MHPSS and livelihoods
assistance, in coordination with service providers.
14. Collaborate with the Medical, Operations, and Protection teams, to support the daily delivery of services related
to migrant arrival, check-ins, identity verification, non-food item (NFI) distribution, room assignment, check-out
procedures, pre-departure logistical arrangements for airport transfers.
15. In coordination with the finance and procurement teams, support the financial and administrative processes of
the DARV, in in line with allocated resources, IOM financial and administrative standards, and in close coordination
with IOM Algeria's relevant units.
16. Contribute suggestions to improve DARV management coordination processes, particularly with OPLA, and
report any challenges immediately to the appropriate supervisor(s).
17. Perform any other tasks that may be assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Political or Social Sciences, International Relations, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Human Rights, Law or related fields from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional
    experience; or,
    • Master's degree in the above-mentioned fields.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Experience in IOM administrative and financial management, budget monitoring, cash management and internal
    control procedures.
    • Experience in working with migrants, refugees, internally displaced persons, victims of trafficking and other
    vulnerable groups.
    • Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government
    institutions/organization in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.

Skills

  • Good understanding of migration-related subject areas dealt with by the Organization;
    • Good communication and interpersonal skills.
    • Personal commitment, drive for results, flexibility and the ability to work effectively and harmoniously with
    colleagues from varied cultures and professional experiences.
    • Knowledge of the usage of office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and knowledge of spreadsheet.

Languages

For this position, fluency in French and English is required (oral and written).
• Knowledge of Arabic, Bambara, Hausa or Germa/Songhai is an advantage.
Working knowledge of any other UN language is an advantage

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports

  • Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.
  • Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.
  • Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.
  • Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction.
  • Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings.

Notes

Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Sr. Research Associate 1, SOM
description:
Current Employees:

If you are a current Staff, Faculty or Temporary employee at the University of Miami, please click here to log in to Workday to use the internal application process. To learn how to apply for a faculty or staff position, please review this tip sheet.

Sr. Research Associate 1

The University of Miami/UHealth department of The Miami Project has an exciting opportunity for a Full Time Sr. Research Associate 1 to work at the UHealth Medical Campus. The Sr. Research Associate 1, SOM (A) provides laboratory-based support for the University’s research activities by tackling the more specialized and complex projects and experiments. Additionally, the incumbent leverages expertise in training and mentoring department staff, students, and less experienced research associates.

CORE JOB SUMMARY

The Sr. Research Associate 1, SOM (A) provides laboratory-based support for the University’s research activities by tackling the more specialized and complex projects and experiments. Additionally, the incumbent leverages expertise in training and mentoring department staff, students, and less experienced research associates.

CORE JOB FUNCTIONS

  • Performs specialized and complex experiments in the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) field.

  • Advances expertise through education, training, and research. Collects, prepares, analyzes, dissects, and evaluates samples for TEM, including resin-embedding block tissue, cell cultures and pellets.

  • Performs sectioning for semi-thin and thin sections in the ultramicrotome.

  • Stains the sections collected onto grids for contrast. Loads nanoparticles and extracellular vesicles onto grids.

  • Specialized tasks to include immunostaining (immunogold) at the TEM level.

  • Operates sensitive and highly complex laboratory equipment such as the ultramicrotomes and the transmission electron microscopes.

  • Acquires images in the transmission electron microscope and sends electronic copies to users.

  • Assists in checking-in users who come to operate the electron microscope independently, including starting the scope and the camera software, and completing the login sheet.

  • Performs quality checks on safety of laboratories, including bio hazards, and insures maintenance of the facilities according to good laboratory practices.

  • Responsible for preparing the laboratories for the annual Environmental Health and Safety inspection.

  • Maintains laboratory equipment in compliance with federal regulations including the two transmission electron microscopes.

  • Contacts technicians to perform necessary repairs.

  • Updates protocols accordingly – both hard copies and electronic files in the shared drive.

  • Assists in training students and volunteers in the standard operating procedures of the Core and equipment specific requirements.

  • Interacts with other laboratories and TEM Core users. Participates in training sessions, workshops and presentations.

  • Adheres to University and unit-level policies and procedures and safeguards University assets.

Department Specific Functions

The Senior RA1 will be responsible for processing samples for transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analyses. This function includes, but it is not limited to, embedding samples (block tissue, cell cultures, pellets, etc.) in resin, sectioning blocks in the ultramicrotome and staining grids. Other specialized duties are loading grids with nanoparticles/extracellular vesicles, immunogold staining for TEM, and operating the two JEOL JEM-1400 electron microscopes. The Senior RA1 will interact with TEM Core users, train students, present at workshops, and assist the Manager in the general maintenance of the laboratory.

This list of duties and responsibilities is not intended to be all-inclusive and may be expanded to include other duties or responsibilities as necessary.

CORE QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master’s Degree in relevant field

  • No experience required. Preference- 3 years of relevant experience in transmission electron microscopy and histology.

  • CEMT certification preferred.

Knowledge, Skills and Attitudes:

  • Skill in collecting, organizing, and analyzing data.

  • Ability to recognize, analyze, and solve a variety of problems.

  • Ability to exercise sound judgment in making critical decisions.

  • Proficient in basic computer operations and Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook).

  • Ability to recognize, analyze, and identify histological tissue.

  • Ability to exercise sound judgment in making critical decisions.

  • Ability to work independently.

  • Ability to operate instruments independently.

The University of Miami offers competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, tuition remission and more.

UHealth-University of Miami Health System, South Florida's only university-based health system, provides leading-edge patient care powered by the ground breaking research and medical education at the Miller School of Medicine. As an academic medical center, we are proud to serve South Florida, Latin America and the Caribbean. Our physicians represent more than 100 specialties and sub-specialties, and have more than one million patient encounters each year. Our tradition of excellence has earned worldwide recognition for outstanding teaching, research and patient care. We're the challenge you've been looking for.

title: Supervisor, Financial Planning
description:
The Corporate Financial Planning group leads Honda Canada's budgeting, forecasting, financial consolidation, management reporting activities, and profitability analysis activities, working closely with Honda Canada senior management, Honda Manufacturing of Canada, American Honda, Honda Motor, and other affiliates. The team supports multiple planning cycles throughout the fiscal year, including budgets, forecasts, and mid-term planning submissions, month-end close and transfer pricing support activities.

The Supervisor leads a team of Financial Analysts responsible for the preparation, consolidation, analysis, and reporting of financial information. This role ensures the accurate and timely delivery of planning, reporting, financial close, while coordinating complex information flows across business units and affiliates. The Supervisor provides technical leadership to the team, challenges assumptions, identifies risks, and supports management decision-making through clear financial insights.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Coordinate and review the preparation of Honda Canada's annual planning cycle, including multiple budgets, forecasts, and multi-year planning submissions, working closely with business units, factories, American Honda, Honda Motor, and other affiliates to validate assumptions, reconcile inputs, and support profitability planning.

  • Coordinate and review the consolidation of financial forecasts and related financial reporting requirements for Honda Canada and Honda Manufacturing of Canada, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and compliance with corporate requirements.

  • Support month-end close activities, including the accurate preparation and review of gross profit variance analyses, incentive accruals, and other key reserves and obligations.

  • Support transfer pricing processes by coordinating financial statement preparation, profitability reporting, and analysis of transfer pricing impacts in collaboration with the Tax function and global affiliates.

  • Lead, coach, and develop the team through clear expectations, regular feedback, and performance reviews.

  • Assign and prioritize work, balance workloads, and monitor milestones to protect delivery dates.

  • Review team deliverables for accuracy and completeness; challenge assumptions and decide when further analysis, correction, or escalation is needed before Manager sign-off.

  • Act as a business partner to stakeholders across the organization.

  • Prepare and review financial analysis, variance explanations, and presentation materials for senior management, translating financial results into clear business insights that support decision-making

  • Lead process and automation improvements that reduce cycle time or manual effort.

  • Maintain the technical capability to execute or back up any major team responsibility.

  • Support system initiatives (SAP S/4HANA) and compliance activities (SOX, audit).

  • Keep the Manager informed of progress, risks, and capacity constraints.

  • Other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Professional accounting designation a must (CPA).
